5.5.s: sutyāyāṃ brahmaṇaḥ prāksubrahmaṇyāyā udgātreṇa samānaṃ karmma
5.5.d: सुत्यायां ब्रह्मणः प्राक्सुब्रह्मण्याया उद्गात्रेण समानं कर्म्म
5.5.m: On the soma-pressing day, the duty of the brahman priest prior to the subrahmaṇyā litany is identical with that of the udgātṛ priest.

The looking at and stepping onto the altar, the movement along the paths, the attendance on the dhiṣṇya hearths, the acceptance of the priestly fees, the consumptions [of soma], and after the unyoking of the stoma, everything other than the singing of the sāman [belongs to him].
However, he should follow along during the consecration offering (dīkṣaṇīyā).
When it has concluded, he should remain seated until the consecration of the patron of the sacrifice.
When the adhvaryu restrains the speech of that [patron], he may then do as he requires.
When they are about to collect [the earth for] the mahāvīra pots, he should sit down silently; when they have been collected, he may do as he requires.

5.5.s: prāyaṇīyāyāssthitāyāṃ yathetanniṣkramya pūrveṇa patnīśālāṃ tiṣṭhedābhihomāt padasya rājakrayaṇyāḥ
5.5.d: प्रायणीयायास्स्थितायां यथेतन्निष्क्रम्य पूर्वेण पत्नीशालां तिष्ठेदाभिहोमात् पदस्य राजक्रयण्याः
5.5.m: When the introductory offering (prāyaṇīyā) has concluded, having gone out as he came, he should stand east of the wife's hut until the offering over the footprint of the cow purchased for the King [Soma].

5.5.s: abhihuta uttareṇa somavahanaṃ gatvā prāgvā padābhihomāddakṣiṇena yatra rājānaṃ kreṣyantaḥ syustatra gatvā tūṣṇīmupaviśet
5.5.d: अभिहुत उत्तरेण सोमवहनं गत्वा प्राग्वा पदाभिहोमाद्दक्षिणेन यत्र राजानं क्रेष्यन्तः स्युस्तत्र गत्वा तूष्णीमुपविशेत्
5.5.m: When the offering has been made, having gone to the north of the cart conveying the soma, or before the offering over the footprint having gone to the south, he should go to where they are about to purchase the King [Soma] and sit down silently.

5.5.s: krīte prāṅutkrāmet paścimenainhṛtvā rājānamādadhyurāhitaṃ pūrveṇa parītyohyamānamanugaccheddakṣiṇena cedgataḥ syāt
5.5.d: क्रीते प्राङुत्क्रामेत् पश्चिमेनैन्हृत्वा राजानमादध्युराहितं पूर्वेण परीत्योह्यमानमनुगच्छेद्दक्षिणेन चेद्गतः स्यात्
5.5.m: When he is purchased, he should step forward towards the east; having carried King [Soma] around to the west, they should place him [in the cart]; if he had gone by the south, having walked around him to the east once placed, he should follow behind as he is conveyed.
If [he had gone] by the north, he should step back towards the west when [Soma] is purchased.
Having carried him to the east, they should place King [Soma].
Having walked around him to the west once placed, he should follow behind as he is conveyed.

5.5.s: tāmevātreṣāmanvāvartteta sā hyasya prāci varttamānasya dakṣiṇeṣā bhavatīti
5.5.d: तामेवात्रेषामन्वावर्त्तेत सा ह्यस्य प्राचि वर्त्तमानस्य दक्षिणेषा भवतीति
5.5.m: He should follow along right beside that cart pole; for as he moves eastwards, that is the southern pole for him—so [it is said].

5.5.s: vimukte cāntareṇa somavahanaṃ patnīśālāñca dakṣiṇotkramya tiṣṭheddīkṣitaścet
5.5.d: विमुक्ते चान्तरेण सोमवहनं पत्नीशालाञ्च दक्षिणोत्क्रम्य तिष्ठेद्दीक्षितश्चेत्
5.5.m: And when it has been unyoked, having stepped out southward between the cart conveying the soma and the wife's hut, he should stand, if consecrated,

5.6.m: He should enter behind King [Soma] as he is being brought inside, not interposing himself with the fire.
If there should be crowding, he may enter even by the southern door.
He should move north of the āhavanīya fire and west of the altar, if consecrated.

5.6.s: tāñcedanavahṛte rājani nirvaperan brāhmaṇrājani samādiśya tatrāsīta
5.6.d: ताञ्चेदनवहृते राजनि निर्वपेरन् ब्राह्मण्राजनि समादिश्य तत्रासीत
5.6.m: If they should perform it before King [Soma] has been taken down, having appointed a brāhmaṇa in place of King [Soma], he should sit there.

5.6.s: tasyāssthitāyāṃ tānūnaptramājyamavamṛśya japeyurhavirasi vaiśvānaramanādhṛṣṭamanādhṛṣyaṃ devānāmojo'nabhiśastyabhiśastipā anabhiśastenyamañjasā satyamuṣageṣsuvitemādhā iti
5.6.d: तस्यास्स्थितायां तानूनप्त्रमाज्यमवमृश्य जपेयुर्हविरसि वैश्वानरमनाधृष्टमनाधृष्यं देवानामोजोऽनभिशस्त्यभिशस्तिपा अनभिशस्तेन्यमञ्जसा सत्यमुषगेष्सुवितेमाधा इति
5.6.m: When that has concluded, touching the tānūnaptra ghee, they should mutter: 'Thou art the oblation, belonging to Vaiśvānara, unassailable, the unassailable might of the gods, protecting against curses, guarding from curse, not to be cursed; rightly, truly, forcefully place me in well-being!'
Having touched water, being addressed by the adhvaryu, he should loosen the King [Soma].

5.6.s: thiraṇyenāntarddhāyābhimṛśeyurśurśuṣṭe deva somāpyāyatāmindrāyaikadhanavida ā tubhyamindraḥ pyāyatāmāsvamindrāya pyāyasvāpyāyayāsmātsukhī sanyāmedhayā svasti te deva soma sutyāmudṛcamaśīyeti
5.6.d: थिरण्येनान्तर्द्धायाभिमृशेयुर्शुर्शुष्टे देव सोमाप्यायतामिन्द्रायैकधनविद आ तुभ्यमिन्द्रः प्यायतामास्वमिन्द्राय प्यायस्वाप्याययास्मात्सुखी सन्यामेधया स्वस्ति ते देव सोम सुत्यामुदृचमशीयेति
5.6.m: Interposing gold, they should touch [him]: 'Shoot by shoot, mayest thou swell, O divine Soma, for Indra, finder of the single prize; may Indra swell for thee; swell thou for Indra; swell for us with wealth and intelligence; may I attain, O divine Soma, the completion of thy pressing in safety!'

5.6.s: kāśamaye prastare nihnuvīrandakṣiṇānuttānān pāṇīn kṛtvā savyānnīca eṣṭā rāya eṣṭā vāmānipreṣe bhagāyarttamṛtavādibhyo namodive namaḥ pṛthivyā iti
5.6.d: काशमये प्रस्तरे निह्नुवीरन्दक्षिणानुत्तानान् पाणीन् कृत्वा सव्यान्नीच एष्टा राय एष्टा वामानिप्रेषे भगायर्त्तमृतवादिभ्यो नमोदिवे नमः पृथिव्या इति
5.6.m: Upon the strew of kāśa grass they should make reverent salutation, turning their right hands upwards and left hands downwards: 'Desirous of wealth, desirous of lovely things, for impulse, for fortune, for truth; reverence to the speakers of truth! Reverence to the sky, reverence to the earth!'

5.6.s: upasadiṣṭirata ūrddhvaṃ tasyāṃ tathaivābhimarśananihnavane savyā aparāhṇa uttānāḥ syurddakṣiṇā nyañcaḥ
5.6.d: उपसदिष्टिरत ऊर्द्ध्वं तस्यां तथैवाभिमर्शननिह्नवने सव्या अपराह्ण उत्तानाः स्युर्द्दक्षिणा न्यञ्चः
5.6.m: Hereafter is the upasad offering; in it the touching and the salutation are in the same manner; in the afternoon the left hands should be turned upwards and the right downwards.
When the upasad libation has been offered with the sruva spoon, he should know that it has concluded.
In a rite having the pravargya ceremony, the gharma offering precedes it.

5.7.s: tamabhīndhiṣyatsu gārhapatyaṃ gatvā yajuṣopaviśeddakṣiṇena dakṣiṇāgnimuttareṇa bahiścet
5.7.d: तमभीन्धिष्यत्सु गार्हपत्यं गत्वा यजुषोपविशेद्दक्षिणेन दक्षिणाग्निमुत्तरेण बहिश्चेत्
5.7.m: When they are about to kindle it, having gone to the gārhapatya fire, he should sit down with a yajus formula: south of the dakṣiṇāgni fire, or to the north if outside.
When it is said, 'The gharma is heated,' standing up they should look upon whichever section the adhvaryu might recite.

5.7.s: thriyamāṇaṃ yathetamanuvrajan japedviśvā āśā dakṣiṇadhaksarvān devānayāḍihasvāhā kṛtasya gharmasya medhoḥ pivatamaścineti
5.7.d: थ्रियमाणं यथेतमनुव्रजन् जपेद्विश्वा आशा दक्षिणधक्सर्वान् देवानयाडिहस्वाहा कृतस्य घर्मस्य मेधोः पिवतमश्चिनेति
5.7.m: Following along as he went while it is being carried, he should mutter: 'Burning the quarters toward the south, thou hast sacrificed to all the gods here; of the gharma offered with svāhā, drink the sweetness, O Aśvins!'

5.7.s: āśrāvita upaviśya japedaśvinā gharmaṃ pātaṃ hārdvānamaharddivābhirūtibhistantrāyiṇe namo dyāvāpṛthivībhyāmiti
5.7.d: आश्रावित उपविश्य जपेदश्विना घर्मं पातं हार्द्वानमहर्द्दिवाभिरूतिभिस्तन्त्रायिणे नमो द्यावापृथिवीभ्यामिति
5.7.m: When the call (āśrāvita) has been made, having sat down, he should mutter: 'O Aśvins, drink the gharma; with your aids protecting the heart day by day; reverence to the performer of the rite, to Heaven and Earth!'

5.7.s: hute yajamānaṃ vācayedapātāmaśvinā gharmamanu dyāvāpṛthivī amsātāmihaiva rātayaḥ santviti
5.7.d: हुते यजमानं वाचयेदपातामश्विना घर्ममनु द्यावापृथिवी अम्सातामिहैव रातयः सन्त्विति
5.7.m: When it is offered, he should make the patron of the sacrifice say: 'The Aśvins have drunk the gharma; Heaven and Earth have approved it; let bounties abide right here!'

5.7.s: gharmaśeṣasya bhakṣayenmadhuhutamindratame'gnāvaśyāma te deva gharma namaste'stu mā mā hsiīriti
5.7.d: घर्मशेषस्य भक्षयेन्मधुहुतमिन्द्रतमेऽग्नावश्याम ते देव घर्म नमस्तेऽस्तु मा मा ह्सिईरिति

5.7.m: If it should be a sacrificial session, the invitation is simply: 'O patrons of the sacrifice, invite!'
Thus he should always perform the pravargya and upasads.
When they are about to take away the stambayajus for the great altar, he should sit down with a yajus formula.
When the cātvāla pit has been demarcated, he may do as he requires.
When they are about to strew the high altar (uttaravedi), he should sit down silently; when it has been strewn, he may do as he requires.

5.7.s: agnicityāyāṃ prāgdīkṣaṇīyāyāḥ sāvitrān homān hoṣyatsu yajuṣopaviśet
5.7.d: अग्निचित्यायां प्राग्दीक्षणीयायाः सावित्रान् होमान् होष्यत्सु यजुषोपविशेत्
5.7.m: In the piling of the fire altar (agniciti), prior to the consecration offering, when they are about to offer the sāvitra libations, he should sit down with a yajus formula.
When those have been offered, he should follow along as the clay for the ukhā pot is being brought.
Having sat while it is being collected, when it has been collected, he may do as he requires.

5.8.m: When they are about to pile the āhavanīya fire, he should sit down with a yajus formula.

5.8.s: tasmin sañcita ukhyāmāsandīṃ nairṛtīśceṣṭakā araṇyhriyamāṇā anugacchet
5.8.d: तस्मिन् सञ्चित उख्यामासन्दीं नैरृतीश्चेष्टका अरण्य्ह्रियमाणा अनुगच्छेत्
5.8.m: When it is piled up, he should follow along as the ukhā pot, the stool, and the nairṛtī bricks are carried into the wilderness.

5.8.s: nidhīyamānānāṃ dakṣiṇataḥ sthitvā nihitāsvapa upaspṛśyānapekṣaṃ pratyāvrajet
5.8.d: निधीयमानानां दक्षिणतः स्थित्वा निहितास्वप उपस्पृश्यानपेक्षं प्रत्याव्रजेत्
5.8.m: Having stood south of them as they are being laid, and having touched water once they are laid down, he should return without looking back.
When they are about to scatter the fire and sow all kinds of herbs, he should sit down silently.

5.8.s: taiḥ sārddhaṃ pratyāvrajya citīḥ praṇīyamānā anugacchet
5.8.d: तैः सार्द्धं प्रत्याव्रज्य चितीः प्रणीयमाना अनुगच्छेत्
5.8.m: Having returned together with them, he should follow along as the layers of bricks are being brought forward.

5.8.s: nidhīyamānānāṃ dakṣiṇataḥ sthitvā nihitāsu dakṣiṇasya pakṣasyāsanno yajuṣopaviśet
5.8.d: निधीयमानानां दक्षिणतः स्थित्वा निहितासु दक्षिणस्य पक्षस्यासन्नो यजुषोपविशेत्
5.8.m: Having stood south of them as they are being laid down, once they are laid, he should sit down near the right wing with a yajus formula.

5.8.s: lokaṃpṛṇāsūpadhīyamānāsu brāhmaṇaṃ tatra samādiśya yathārthsyāditi śāṇḍilyaḥ
5.8.d: लोकंपृणासूपधीयमानासु ब्राह्मणं तत्र समादिश्य यथार्थ्स्यादिति शाण्डिल्यः
5.8.m: When the lokaṃpṛṇā bricks are being laid, having appointed a brāhmaṇa there, he may do as he requires, says Śāṇḍilya.
He should simply remain seated, says Dhānañjayya.
When they are about to perform the rites of the completed pile, he should remain seated, rising only as needed.
He should follow behind the samrāj stool as it is being carried.

5.8.s: pariṣicyamāne'pa upaspṛśya taiḥ sārddhaṃ pratyābrajyāgniṃ praṇīyamānamanugacchedapratirathaṃ japstūṣṇīmanagnicityā cet
5.8.d: परिषिच्यमानेऽप उपस्पृश्य तैः सार्द्धं प्रत्याब्रज्याग्निं प्रणीयमानमनुगच्छेदप्रतिरथं जप्स्तूष्णीमनग्निचित्या चेत्
5.8.m: When water is being sprinkled around, having touched water and returned together with them, he should follow along as the fire is being brought forward, muttering the Apratiratha hymn, or silently if there is no fire altar piling.

5.8.s: nidhīyamānasya dakṣiṇataḥ sthitvā nihite dakṣiṇā bahirvedi yajuṣopaviśet
5.8.d: निधीयमानस्य दक्षिणतः स्थित्वा निहिते दक्षिणा बहिर्वेदि यजुषोपविशेत्
5.8.m: Having stood south of it as it is being placed, once placed, he should sit down with a yajus formula to the south outside the altar,
When the two havirdhāna carts are being rolled forward, he should follow them.
When they are enclosed, he should go right there and sit down.
When the audumbarī post has been erected, he may do as he pleases, he may do as he pleases.

5.9.m: When they are about to bring forward Agni and Soma, he should step onto the altar with a mantra.
Passing behind the uttaravedi towards the north, he should mutter the altar-stepping formula near the cātvāla pit, if he is consecrated.
From then on, the stepping onto the altar is silent.

5.9.s: krītvā rājā yenātihṛtaḥ syāttena gatvā tūṣṇīmupaviśet
5.9.d: क्रीत्वा राजा येनातिहृतः स्यात्तेन गत्वा तूष्णीमुपविशेत्
5.9.m: Having bought [King Soma], he should go by the path along which the King was carried past, and sit down silently.

5.9.s: rājānharetyuktaḥ pūrveṇāgnimekasmā atipradāya tān prasavyaṃ parītyādāyānugaccheddakṣiṇena cedgataḥ syāt
5.9.d: राजान्हरेत्युक्तः पूर्वेणाग्निमेकस्मा अतिप्रदाय तान् प्रसव्यं परीत्यादायानुगच्छेद्दक्षिणेन चेद्गतः स्यात्
5.9.m: When addressed with, 'Carry King Soma,' having handed him over to someone to the east of the fire, he should walk around them from right to left, take him, and follow, if he had gone by the south.
If he had gone by the north, he should walk around the fire as he had come, take him, and follow.

5.9.s: anyena cedbrahmā vrajitaḥ syādanyena rājā tenainaṃ pragṛhṇīyāt
5.9.d: अन्येन चेद्ब्रह्मा व्रजितः स्यादन्येन राजा तेनैनं प्रगृह्णीयात्
5.9.m: If the brahman priest has walked by one way and the King by another, he should take hold of him by that [path].
These indeed are the two options for the brahman priest's movement, even when he carries [Soma].
He should sit in the āgnīdhra shed while the two oblations are being offered, says Dhānañjayya.
He should follow the King and the clarified butters as they are carried north of the āgnīdhra shed.
When they have entered, he should go behind the havirdhāna shed and sit down, says Gautama.
To the east, says Śāṇḍilyāyana, in front of the southern doorpost with a formula.
When the omentum of the agnīṣomīya victim has been offered, he should pass towards the north as he had come and sprinkle himself at the cātvāla pit.

In this very same way, in the latter part of the night when the clarified butters have entered, takes place the sitting down, and the sprinkling when the omentum of the savanīya victim has been offered.

5.10.m: If he is consecrated, he should touch all the iḍā portions.

5.10.s: vasatīvarīṣu parihriyamāṇāsu dakṣiṇotkramya tiṣṭhedadīkṣitaścedā tāsāṃ pariharaṇāt
5.10.d: वसतीवरीषु परिह्रियमाणासु दक्षिणोत्क्रम्य तिष्ठेददीक्षितश्चेदा तासां परिहरणात्
5.10.m: While the vasatīvarī waters are being carried around, he should step out to the south and stand until they have been carried around, if he is not consecrated.
He should follow King Soma as he is carried to the āgnīdhra shed.

5.10.s: nidhīyamānasya dakṣiṇataḥ sthitvā nihite yathārth syāt
5.10.d: निधीयमानस्य दक्षिणतः स्थित्वा निहिते यथार्थ् स्यात्
5.10.m: Having stood to the south of him while he is being placed down, he may do as he pleases once he is placed.
If he is consecrated, he should lie down right there.

5.10.s: apararātra ājyāni grahīṣyataḥ pūveṇa gatvāgniñca paścimena vā yajuṣopaviśet
5.10.d: अपररात्र आज्यानि ग्रहीष्यतः पूवेण गत्वाग्निञ्च पश्चिमेन वा यजुषोपविशेत्
5.10.m: In the latter part of the night, when [the adhvaryu] is about to draw the clarified butters, he should go to the east and behind the fire, or sit down with a formula.

5.10.s: ātteṣu prāṅutkramya prasavyaṃ parītyānugacchetpūrveṇa cedgataḥ syāt
5.10.d: आत्तेषु प्राङुत्क्रम्य प्रसव्यं परीत्यानुगच्छेत्पूर्वेण चेद्गतः स्यात्
5.10.m: When they have been taken, he should step out towards the east, go around from right to left, and follow, if he had gone by the east.
If by the west, he should go around the fire as he had come and follow.
Only while the clarified butters are about to be drawn should he sit down here, says Śāṇḍilya.

5.10.s: adhvaryaṇokto vācaṃ yacchedā tṛtīyaṃ prātaranuvākasya prathamāyāḥ
5.10.d: अध्वर्यणोक्तो वाचं यच्छेदा तृतीयं प्रातरनुवाकस्य प्रथमायाः
5.10.m: When addressed by the adhvaryu, he should restrain his speech until the third [verse] of the first hymn of the morning litany;
or until the oblation of the upāṃśu and antaryāma cups;

5.10.s: havirddhānañcet pūrveṇa gataḥ syādupāśvantaryāmau hoṣyatsūdaṅṅatikramya tiṣṭhedadīkṣitaścet
5.10.d: हविर्द्धानञ्चेत् पूर्वेण गतः स्यादुपाश्वन्तर्यामौ होष्यत्सूदङ्ङतिक्रम्य तिष्ठेददीक्षितश्चेत्
5.10.m: If he has gone east of the havirdhāna shed, he should step out towards the north and stand when they are about to offer the upāṃśu and antaryāma cups, if he is not consecrated,
When they glide forth [for the bahiṣpavamāna], he should take hold from behind.
His ritual act is identical with the prastotṛ priest's prior to sitting down.
Having reached the chanting place, he should sit down facing the prastotṛ priest with a formula, without sitting too close.

5.11.m: The two sections beginning with 'You are a ray' are the stomabhāga formulas.
With them, he should bless each of the stotras separately in succession, when addressed with: 'O brahman priest, we will chant, O director!'

5.11.s: ūrddhvaṃ prathamādrātriparyyāyādyatra syādamuṣmai tveti taṃ jinveti tatra brūyāt
5.11.d: ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रथमाद्रात्रिपर्य्यायाद्यत्र स्यादमुष्मै त्वेति तं जिन्वेति तत्र ब्रूयात्
5.11.m: After the first night-round, wherever it occurs, he should say 'to so-and-so thee' and 'quicken him' there.
'Spurred by Savitṛ, flow forth to Bṛhaspati!' is the ending of each one;
He may add 'Bhūḥ bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Bṛhaspati is the brahman priest; I am the human one. Om!', or just the syllable 'Om'.
He should bless the junction according to the traditional text.

5.11.s: traidhaṃ vibhajediti dhānañjayyo vasuko'si vaspaṣṭirasi veṣaśrīrasi vasukāya tvā vaspaṣṭaye tvā veṣaśriye tvā vasukaṃ jinva vaspaṣṭiṃ jinva veṣaśriyaṃ jinva savitṛprasūtā vṛhaspataye sruteti
5.11.d: त्रैधं विभजेदिति धानञ्जय्यो वसुकोऽसि वस्पष्टिरसि वेषश्रीरसि वसुकाय त्वा वस्पष्टये त्वा वेषश्रिये त्वा वसुकं जिन्व वस्पष्टिं जिन्व वेषश्रियं जिन्व सवितृप्रसूता वृहस्पतये स्रुतेति
5.11.m: He should divide it threefold, says Dhānañjayya: 'You are Vasuka, you are Vaspaṣṭi, you are Veṣaśrī; to Vasuka thee, to Vaspaṣṭi thee, to Veṣaśrī thee; quicken Vasuka, quicken Vaspaṣṭi, quicken Veṣaśrī; spurred by Savitṛ, flow forth to Bṛhaspati!'

5.11.s: sruta devena savitrā prasūtā ityanumantrayeta mānasaṃ vājapeye ca bṛhat
5.11.d: स्रुत देवेन सवित्रा प्रसूता इत्यनुमन्त्रयेत मानसं वाजपेये च बृहत्
5.11.m: He should bless the mānasa chant, and the bṛhat at the Vājapeya sacrifice, with: 'Flow forth, spurred by the god Savitṛ!'
The stotras [arising] from an increase [are blessed] with the preceding one, because of its increase;
or with the subsequent one, because of desiring that;
or like the mānasa chant, because of the common characteristic of being redundant;
or with a blessing over all, because none is specifically stated.
Whichever stotra might be omitted, [it is omitted] together with its stomabhāga formula.
When the bahiṣpavamāna chant has been praised, he should go right there and sit down.
When the omentum has been offered, after having sprinkled himself and worshipped the dhiṣṇya hearths, the sitting down in the sadas takes place as explained.

5.12.m: He should restrain his speech during the chant and recitation.
and everywhere when [a recitation] is being recited.
Having stepped out from the concluding purificatory bath, he should follow the remainder of the sacrifice.

5.12.s: ahargaṇeṣven sadātipraiṣeṇa praśāstā vācaṃ yamayati rājānrakṣeti cāha tadubhayaṃ kuryādā vasatīvarīṇāṃ pariharaṇāt
5.12.d: अहर्गणेष्वेन् सदातिप्रैषेण प्रशास्ता वाचं यमयति राजान्रक्षेति चाह तदुभयं कुर्यादा वसतीवरीणां परिहरणात्
5.12.m: In sacrifices with groups of days, the praśāstṛ priest restrains speech with an intensive command, saying: 'Protect the Soma-King!' He should do both until the carrying around of the vasatīvarī waters.
In a sacrificial session they should do that by rotation.

5.12.s: vājapeye pṛṣṭhasya stotramanumantrya sadasyaṃ brahmāsana upaveśya niṣkrāmet
5.12.d: वाजपेये पृष्ठस्य स्तोत्रमनुमन्त्र्य सदस्यं ब्रह्मासन उपवेश्य निष्क्रामेत्
5.12.m: In the Vājapeya, after chanting along to the stotra of the pṛṣṭha laud and seating the sadasya priest on the seat of the brahman priest, he should step out.
To the east of the Āgnīdhra shed, a post should be set into the ground.
To the south of the mārjālīya hut, inside the altar ground, according to Śāṇḍilya.
Upon it, a seventeen-spoked chariot wheel of udumbara wood should be mounted.
In its absence, whatever chariot wheel [is available].

5.12.s: tasmin bāhū ādadhyāddevasyāh savituḥ prasave satyasavaso bṛhaspatervājito vājajito varṣiṣṭhamadhi nāk ruheyamiti
5.12.d: तस्मिन् बाहू आदध्याद्देवस्याह् सवितुः प्रसवे सत्यसवसो बृहस्पतेर्वाजितो वाजजितो वर्षिष्ठमधि नाक् रुहेयमिति
5.12.m: He should place his two arms upon it with: 'At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, whose impulse is true, may I, with the prize of prize-winning Bṛhaspati, mount the highest firmament!'
While the chariots run in the race, he should sing 'āvirmaryāḥ...', omitting the syllable ā at the beginning of the udgītha.
In its place, having substituted the two-syllable word 'agman', when they have departed.
As handed down in the text while they run toward [the goal] or have run out.
Or as handed down in the text everywhere.

5.12.s: parivarttayan gāyetparivarttya gāyedgītvā vā parivarttayedgāyato vānyaḥ parivarttayet
5.12.d: परिवर्त्तयन् गायेत्परिवर्त्त्य गायेद्गीत्वा वा परिवर्त्तयेद्गायतो वान्यः परिवर्त्तयेत्
5.12.m: He should sing while turning [the wheel], or sing after turning it, or turn it after singing, or someone else should turn it while he sings.

5.12.s: udaṅṅavarohaṃ manyeta viṣṇoḥ kramo'si viṣṇoḥ krāntamasi viṣṇorvikrāntamasīti
5.12.d: उदङ्ङवरोहं मन्येत विष्णोः क्रमोऽसि विष्णोः क्रान्तमसि विष्णोर्विक्रान्तमसीति
5.12.m: He should consider descending towards the north with: 'You are the stride of Viṣṇu; you are the stepped step of Viṣṇu; you are the wide stride of Viṣṇu.'
Turning around to the south, he should enter the sadas.

5.12.s: tatrāsīno hiraṇyaṃ madhu ca nānā pratigṛhṇīyāt
5.12.d: तत्रासीनो हिरण्यं मधु च नाना प्रतिगृह्णीयात्
5.12.m: Seated there, he should receive gold and honey separately.
And in the Ṛtapeya, a cup as the sacrificial gift.
He should give the honey to a brāhmaṇa, and lay down the gold.
With the triṣṭubh metre, he should consume the cup, consuming the entire [contents].

5.12.s: taṃ pratigṛhṇīyāditi sthaviro gautamaḥ kastvā dadāti sa tvā dadāti kasmai tvā dadāti tasmai tvā dadāti kastvā kaṃ bhakṣayāmīti bhakṣayedvāgdevī sīmasya tṛpyatviti vā tṛpyatviti vā
5.12.d: तं प्रतिगृह्णीयादिति स्थविरो गौतमः कस्त्वा ददाति स त्वा ददाति कस्मै त्वा ददाति तस्मै त्वा ददाति कस्त्वा कं भक्षयामीति भक्षयेद्वाग्देवी सीमस्य तृप्यत्विति वा तृप्यत्विति वा
5.12.m: He should receive it [with the formula], so says the elder Gautama: 'Who gives you? He gives you. To whom does he give you? To him he gives you. Who [are] you? Whom do I consume?' Or he should consume it with: 'May the goddess Vāc be satisfied with its extract!' or with: 'May she be satisfied!'

6.1.m: The santani chant, being prescribed, [is applied] to each verse separately, not across all, because of the generation of the stoma.
And likewise other [sāmans] in their own various metres.
The santani chant [is used] just like the vāhiṣṭhīya chant.
Or in three triplets, like single verses, because it is seen in a triplet.
And because the number of the stoma [is achieved] through the sāman.
And the text says: 'He sings continuously.'
And it is extracted on single verses in the ritual manual.
The occurrence in a triplet is for the purpose of a standard of measure; the conclusion of the sāman belongs to the strophic verse.
In all of them there should be preludes, by virtue of the general rule and the practice of the pragātha stanza.
Not on the two subsequent verses, say the teachers, on account of tradition.
And because of the text 'He sings continuously', an omission of liturgical divisions is seen.
Its prelude occurs at the beginning of the stotra, or in the repetitions, or at the beginnings of the rounds.
'Everywhere on the first [verse],' says Dhānañjayya.
Those that consist of cadences and have responses are not to be preluded.

6.1.s: dhānañjayyena prathamāyāśāṇḍilya uttare tu stotrīye viṣṭāvamukheṣvevāprastāvye viṣṭāveṣu caikiṣu trivṛtstome ca parivarttinī vidhānam
6.1.d: धानञ्जय्येन प्रथमायाशाण्डिल्य उत्तरे तु स्तोत्रीये विष्टावमुखेष्वेवाप्रस्ताव्ये विष्टावेषु चैकिषु त्रिवृत्स्तोमे च परिवर्त्तिनी विधानम्
6.1.m: With Dhānañjayya [regarding] the first [verse]; Śāṇḍilya [holds] that the two subsequent strophic verses are not to be preluded only at the openings of the strophic shifts, and in the strophic shifts of single-verse chants, and in the ninefold stoma, the rule is turning around.
There is disagreement regarding the metre of the two subsequent strophic verses.
They should be dvipadā verses when not preluded; kakubh verses when preluded.
Śāṇḍilya says they are bṛhatī verses; kakubh verses when not preluded.
If so, both are kakubh verses, says the elder Gautama.
Both are bṛhatī verses, says Dhānañjayya.

6.2.m: The arrangement of stomas is performed with the first strophic arrangements, when not specified.
They are the standard ones and serve all purposes.
Or he should arrange them according to the desired blessing.
Some consider the second [arrangement] of the ninefold stoma to be standard, for the first ones have no strophic shifts.
And it does not apply to the śāra, śiras, sandhi, and santani chants.
And in this [stoma there is the formula]: 'May rain, however, not fall...'
The transposition of the iṣu stoma occurs by means of the two iṣu arrangements.
The earlier of the two belongs to the agniṣṭoma chant of the Falcon sacrifice.
In sacrificial sessions, one should employ all of them during the ten-day period.
'Having set aside those intended for malevolent rites,' says Śāṇḍilya.
Śāṇḍilyāyana says: '[and] the kulāyinī arrangement.'
One should arrange the Hotṛ's sāmans on regular [stoma-forms] and the other [sāmans] on non-regular ones.

6.2.s: tathā kurvan prāgāthikāni parivarttinyā prathamasyeti śāṇḍilyaḥ
6.2.d: तथा कुर्वन् प्रागाथिकानि परिवर्त्तिन्या प्रथमस्येति शाण्डिल्यः
6.2.m: When doing so, [one should arrange] the pragātha-based [sāmans] on the revolving [stoma-form] of the first [day], so says Śāṇḍilya.

6.2.s: sakṛtsarvāḥ samāpya pathyayaiva tata ūrddhvamiti dhānañjayyaḥ
6.2.d: सकृत्सर्वाः समाप्य पथ्ययैव तत ऊर्द्ध्वमिति धानञ्जय्यः
6.2.m: Having completed all of them once, [one should proceed] from then onward only with the regular [stoma-form], so says Dhānañjayya.

6.2.s: asamāptāsu tvapi hotṛṣāma pathyayaiva tathā kuryyāt
6.2.d: असमाप्तासु त्वपि होतृषाम पथ्ययैव तथा कुर्य्यात्
6.2.m: Even when they are not completed, however, one should arrange the Hotṛ's sāman only with the regular [stoma-form].

6.2.s: kulāyinīṃ cet prayuñjīta prathamasyāhno dvitīyaṃ pṛṣṭhantayā vidadhyāt
6.2.d: कुलायिनीं चेत् प्रयुञ्जीत प्रथमस्याह्नो द्वितीयं पृष्ठन्तया विदध्यात्
6.2.m: If one should employ the Kulāyinī [stoma-form], one should arrange the second pṛṣṭha laud of the first day with it.
One should arrange the final uktha laud of the sixth day with the highest viṣṭuti of the thirty-three-fold [stoma].
The application has been declared by the Brāhmaṇa in the forty-four-fold [stoma].
The earlier application is pressing-conforming; the later is stotra-conforming.
One should do so in that which belongs to [its specific] day.
With the subsequent [viṣṭuti] of the forty-eight-fold [stoma], one should arrange only the ājya [stotra] of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest;
or all the Hotraka priests' sāmans everywhere;
or in the middle [stotra] of each of the soma-pressing sessions;
In sattras that are not ten-night periods, only regular [stoma-forms are used], so says Gautama.
All [forms are used], so says Dhānañjayya.

6.3.m: In the absence of a specific instruction, the rule for triplet hymns is by the citation of the beginning [verse].
In the final verse of the triplet, [the citation is] in reverse order;
The bahiṣpavamāna chant of the Ekatrika [sacrifice] has semen [verses].
In the Udbhid [sacrifice], the corresponding verse is a single verse, so says Śāṇḍilya.
[It is] the strophic verse, so say Gautama and Dhānañjayya.
The final two triplets [are used] in the bahiṣpavamāna chant in the Cāturmāsya sacrifices;
The triplet-formation of the vāmadevya, yajñāyajñīya, and forest-sung melodies, and the former ones of the pṛṣṭha lauds, occurs in the two subsequent pavamāna chants,
and there is no prohibition of others.
When making [a chant out of] one single verse, one should make it on the first [verse] from the beginning;
three in a single triplet, on different strophic verses;
of four, two on the first, the other two separately on the subsequent two [verses].
At the midday pressing, when that [happens], one or two [are placed] on the bṛhatī verse alone;
three should be accommodated on both;
if it is without an added verse, [one should place] one of the two on the gāyatrī verse, so says Dhānañjayya.
Both [should be placed] on the bṛhatī verse, so says Śāṇḍilya.
If it is with an added verse, one [should be placed] at the end on the added verse alone;
two on it and from the beginning: that is arranged like a hare's ear;
when there are three, the added verse is dropped;
four [should be placed] on different strophic verses.
In the twelve-day sacrifice, the sāmans of the bṛhatī verse form a triplet.
At the third pressing, if there is one, [it is placed] on the anuṣṭubh verse;
[when there are] two or more, [they are placed] in immediate succession beginning with the kakubh verse.
The triplet nature and single-verse nature of the uṣṇih and kakubh verses [are determined] without conflict.

6.4.s: vāmadevyantu tṛce viśvajicchilpe yajñāyajñīyaprabhṛtīni ca trīṇi
6.4.d: वामदेव्यन्तु तृचे विश्वजिच्छिल्पे यज्ञायज्ञीयप्रभृतीनि च त्रीणि
6.4.m: The vāmadevya melody, however, is on a triplet in the Viśvajit-śilpa rite, and the three beginning with the yajñāyajñīya melody [are also on triplets].
When the stoma allows, the last [sāman] everywhere is on a triplet.
If the second [sāman] is to be sung in the forest,
in its absence, that which is prior to the last [is on a triplet].

6.4.s: ekarcasthāneṣvanāpadyamānāni tṛceṣu kuryyāt gāyatraṃ triṇidhanaṃ madhyandine madhye nidhanamaiḍamārbhave
6.4.d: एकर्चस्थानेष्वनापद्यमानानि तृचेषु कुर्य्यात् गायत्रं त्रिणिधनं मध्यन्दिने मध्ये निधनमैडमार्भवे
6.4.m: Those that are not provided for in the positions of single verses, one should perform on triplets: the gāyatra melody with three cadences, [and] at the midday pressing, [the melody with] a cadence in the middle, [and] the melody with an iḍā-cadence at the third pressing.
One should arrange those [sāmans] whose triplet- or single-verse status is not specified by this direction.
Where the kakubh verse at the midday pressing is a single verse, [the sāman is placed] on it, except in the highest vrātyastoma sacrifice.
In the first two vrātyastoma sacrifices, at the third pressing, the gāyatra melody is on a single verse, [and] the Maruts' chant with stobha interjection on a triplet, so says Dhānañjayya.
In repetitions of four-verse hymns, one should remove the last [verse].
[He should omit] the third [verse] of the sarvasvāra and the svarasāman [days].
Of the [hymn beginning with] "pra vām arcanti", [he should omit] the second [verse].
In the [hymn beginning with] "suṣamiddhaḥ", [he should use] the verse addressed to Tanūnapāt for the Atris, Vasiṣṭhas, Śunakas, Kaṇvas, Saṃkṛtis, and Vadhryaśvas;
In case of conflict [among them], however, the ritual procedure belongs to the majority,
or the sacrificial participants conform to the master of the house — so it is understood.

6.5.s: varddhamāneṣu stomeṣu prathamasya paryyāyasya prathamā tṛcabhāgā tasyāstrirvacanam
6.5.d: वर्द्धमानेषु स्तोमेषु प्रथमस्य पर्य्यायस्य प्रथमा तृचभागा तस्यास्त्रिर्वचनम्
6.5.m: In increasing stomas, the first triplet-part verse belongs to the first round: its chanting is threefold;
In the middle [round, the order is] the concluding verse, the triplet-part verse, and the insertion place;
in the last [round, it is] the insertion place, the concluding verse, and the triplet-part verse.
In the absence of that, the rounds would stand in the positions of the triplet-part verses,
There are no rounds consisting of a single [verse].
In [stomas with rounds of] equal [numbers], the performance of the strophic verses is equal.
In those exceeding by one [verse], there is one extra; two in those exceeding by two;
They proceed by an increase of two [verses] from even and odd [numbers].
The odd [stomas] begin with one; the even begin with two.
By an increase of three, both have equality and inequality.
Those beginning with one exceed by one;
those beginning with two exceed by two;
those beginning with three are equal.
The unequal [stomas] proceed through equal rounds.
He should bring together the rounds of the two immediately adjacent equal [stomas] on either side:
one [round] of the preceding [stoma] in those exceeding by one,
Among them, for the even [stomas] exceeding by one, the first two rounds are odd;
for those exceeding by two, the latter two [rounds are odd].
The reverse [applies] to even and odd [rounds] in the odd [stomas].
He should perform the rounds in their proper place; that is without defect.

6.6.m: With whatever [verse] the preceding round ends, with that the subsequent one begins;
Likewise, where an ascent of rounds is not possible in all, he should make only melody-symmetry;
but he should avoid a descent of rounds,

6.6.s: prathamāyāḥ prayoge bhūyiṣṭhe brahmāyatanīyā madhyamāyāḥ kṣattrāyatanīyottamāyā viḍāyatanīyā
6.6.d: प्रथमायाः प्रयोगे भूयिष्ठे ब्रह्मायतनीया मध्यमायाः क्षत्त्रायतनीयोत्तमाया विडायतनीया
6.6.m: When the repetition of the first [verse] is in the majority, it is a brāhmaṇa-suited arrangement; of the middle, a kṣatriya-suited arrangement; of the last, a vaiśya-suited arrangement.
In forming rounds for [stomas other than] those of the Ten-Night rite, he should collect only regular rounds;
in the absence of specific instruction, however, [he should use] those of the revolving trivṛt [stoma].

6.6.s: ekinyāvarttisthānagate triṣpurastāddhiṃkār śāṇḍilyaḥ trike ca prathamayā stomapūraṇam
6.6.d: एकिन्यावर्त्तिस्थानगते त्रिष्पुरस्ताद्धिंकार् शाण्डिल्यः त्रिके च प्रथमया स्तोमपूरणम्
6.6.m: When a single [verse] falls into the place of an āvṛtti, Śāṇḍilya says there are three hiṅkāra syllables in front, and in a triad the completion of the stoma is made with the first [verse].
Dhānañjayya says [it is made] with a triplet, and the hiṅkāra syllable is uttered only once for a single [verse].
Bhāṇḍitāyana says that with the rounds of the fifteen-verse stoma, he should arrange the rounds of the night separately in order, when it is passed over.

6.6.s: tatra viṣṭāvāḥ paryyāyasthāneṣu syuḥ pṛthak ca stotrīyāsu paryāyāḥ
6.6.d: तत्र विष्टावाः पर्य्यायस्थानेषु स्युः पृथक् च स्तोत्रीयासु पर्यायाः
6.6.m: There, the strophic shifts should be in the places of the rounds, and the rounds [should be] separately in the strophic verses.

6.6.s: dāśarātrikebhya ekayā jyāyaḥsu tasmāt pūrvasyottame paryāya āvapet
6.6.d: दाशरात्रिकेभ्य एकया ज्यायःसु तस्मात् पूर्वस्योत्तमे पर्याय आवपेत्
6.6.m: In stomas greater by one than those of the Ten-Night rite, he should insert [the additional verse] in the last round of the preceding one;
in these, however, [the arrangement should be] brāhmaṇa-suited or kṣatriya-suited.
Gautama says there is skipping over in the forty-verse [stoma];

6.7.m: In a ten-verse [stoma], there is a tetrad in the middle, and the rounds of the revolving [trivṛt] on either side.
If one performs the brāhmaṇa-suited arrangement with two udyatī rounds, one should make a four-verse group on the first [verse].
In the twelve-[verse stoma], there are two-verse strophic shifts in the places of the triplet-part verses.

6.7.s: trayodaśatrayovśiyoḥ pañcavśie ca madhyamaḥ paryāyo jyāyānekajyāyaḥsu kanīyānekakanīyaḥsu
6.7.d: त्रयोदशत्रयोव्शियोः पञ्चव्शिए च मध्यमः पर्यायो ज्यायानेकज्यायःसु कनीयानेककनीयःसु

6.7.m: In the first of them, the [shifts] are even and uneven, says Śāṇḍilyāyana.
In both, it is according to the inherent form, says Dhānañjayya.
In the eighteen-[verse stoma], one should insert [the additional verse] into the seventeen-[verse stoma] itself, says Gautama.
It should be arranged according to the general rule, says Dhānañjayya.
In it, there is a threefold chanting of the first [verse], and likewise of the last.

6.7.s: pañcadaśa paryāyāvabhito navī madhye trikaviṣṭāva iti dhānañjayyaḥ
6.7.d: पञ्चदश पर्यायावभितो नवी मध्ये त्रिकविष्टाव इति धानञ्जय्यः
6.7.m: There are two fifteen-[verse] rounds on either side and a nine-[verse round] in the middle, having three-verse strophic shifts, says Dhānañjayya.
Śāṇḍilyāyana, however, [holds that it is] according to the inherent form.
Even when assigned to an [independent] day, [it should be performed] with the first only, says Śāṇḍilya.

6.8.m: In the two four-stoma sacrifices, there are four rounds.

6.8.s: tatra catuṣke dvau prathamāyāṃ paryāyau syātāṃ yadi brahmāyatanīyāṃ kuryāt
6.8.d: तत्र चतुष्के द्वौ प्रथमायां पर्यायौ स्यातां यदि ब्रह्मायतनीयां कुर्यात्
6.8.m: There, in the four-verse group, there should be two rounds on the first [verse] if one would make the brāhmaṇa-suited arrangement.
On the middle [verse], if [one would make] the kṣatriya-suited arrangement.
Likewise in the eight-[verse stoma]; but its rounds are two-verse [groups].

6.8.s: pūrvayoḥ pūrva uttarayoruttara evaṃ vihitāvaparāviti śāṇḍilyaḥ
6.8.d: पूर्वयोः पूर्व उत्तरयोरुत्तर एवं विहितावपराविति शाण्डिल्यः
6.8.m: The former [round falls] on the two former [verses], the latter on the two latter; the other two are arranged in this way, says Śāṇḍilya.
The second [round falls] on the two former [verses], and the other on distinct strophic verses, says Dhānañjayya.

6.8.s: dvādaśe vyākhyātau prathamottamau madhyamau dvikau pūrvayoḥ pūrva uttarayoruttaraḥ
6.8.d: द्वादशे व्याख्यातौ प्रथमोत्तमौ मध्यमौ द्विकौ पूर्वयोः पूर्व उत्तरयोरुत्तरः
6.8.m: In the twelve-[verse stoma], the first and last [rounds] have been explained; the middle two are two-verse groups: the former on the two former [verses], the latter on the two latter.
In the sixteen-[verse stoma], there are four rounds of the twelve-[verse stoma]; of them, the two middle ones are alike.
In the twenty-four-[verse stoma], there are four six-verse rounds, with two-verse strophic shifts.
The rounds should fall upon distinct triplets.

6.8.s: yajñāyajñīyarkṣu vā prathamaḥ prathamāsu ca yajñāyajñīyaprathamāyāsākamaśvarkṣu paramadhyamayośca dvitīyaḥ pūrvayośca madhyamayorhārivarṇarkṣu tairaścyottamāyāñca tṛtīyaḥ pūrveṣāñcottamāsu tairaścyarkṣu cāntyaḥ
6.8.d: यज्ञायज्ञीयर्क्षु वा प्रथमः प्रथमासु च यज्ञायज्ञीयप्रथमायासाकमश्वर्क्षु परमध्यमयोश्च द्वितीयः पूर्वयोश्च मध्यमयोर्हारिवर्णर्क्षु तैरश्च्योत्तमायाञ्च तृतीयः पूर्वेषाञ्चोत्तमासु तैरश्च्यर्क्षु चान्त्यः
6.8.m: Or the first [round falls] on the verses of the yajñāyajñīya melody, and on the first verses [of the triplets]; the second on the first [verse] of the yajñāyajñīya melody, on the verses of the sākamaśva melody, and on the other middle [verses], and on the middle two of the former [triplets]; the third on the verses of the hārivarṇa melody and on the last verse of the tairaścya melody; and the last on the last verses of the former [triplets] and on the verses of the tairaścya melody.
Or the penultimate has two-verse strophic shifts; in the horse sacrifice, the others [are modified], beginning with the eighteen-[verse stoma].
Or the two fifteen-[verse] rounds are former, and the two twenty-one-[verse rounds] are latter; or the two latter.

6.9.m: They declare the combinations of meter, deity, and sāman-endings to be regular, as in the case of the jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice that possesses the ṣoḍaśin [stotra] and the atirātra sacrifice.
In the last uktha [stotra], anuṣṭubh meters are regular.
Different meters, however, [occur] on account of explicit injunction.
The deity in whose honor the verses chanted are dedicated is the deity of the stotra.
The observation of exceptions is according to each lesson.
The independent-tone [sāmans] are those that have a hāi-syllable independent tone, a word independent tone, or a nasalized tone.
Other than these, and other than those having iḍā and vāc as cadence, [sāmans] possess cadences.
When all coincide in identity, there is monotony, except in the case of vāc.
From the ten-night rite, those [rites] belonging to the six-day period, and these of the eighth and ninth days, follow the procedure of the multi-day sacrifice.
And the [rites] of the jyotis and the go follow the procedure of the one-day sacrifice.
Where verses and sāmans that resemble the ritual manual come together, that is the procedure for benediction, as in malevolent rites.
In the two latter [pressings], the opening verses of the pressing session are gāyatrī verses, says Śaucivṛkṣi.
[They are] those of the midday pressing, say the teachers.
In multi-day sacrifices beginning with the two-night rite, before the six-day periods, the last [day] follows the procedure of the one-day sacrifice, says the son of Rāṇāyanī.
All follow the procedure of the multi-day sacrifice, says Vaiyāghrapadya.
Lāmakāyana, however, [holds that there is] a combination of multi-day and one-day procedures.

6.10.m: A pause marks the end of the prastāva of indivisible [sāmans].
In the first vāravantīya melody, it consists of four syllables.
And of the kārṇaśravasa, ājiga, and surūpa melodies.
[It is] a verse quarter in the case of the vājiga and others.
The [nidhana] of the nānada [sāman] consists of sixteen syllables.
Likewise in the gośṛṅga and sañjaya [sāmans], and that which is the daivodāsa [sāman] in the night [service].
That of the raivata ṛṣabha [sāman] consists of thirty-six syllables.
The taking up of the udgītha of all [sāmans] is with the syllable om.
However, Dhānañjayya holds that there is omission of the first syllable [of the verse].
In [verses] beginning with a vowel, one should turn that very vowel into the syllable om; in those beginning with a consonant, the syllable om is an insertion.
However, one should apply [om] as an insertion everywhere.
Dhānañjayya says: uttering the sound clearly, not separated, not delayed, without nasalisation, supported in the chest, and not clashing the teeth, one should chant the udgītha.
Of visible, invisible, quick, slow, placed, raised, drawn out, and undrawn out [accents or notes], one should perform that by which he can sing musically.
The beginning of a quarter-verse is the place of the pratihāra everywhere.
When a quarter-verse is not specified, [it is taken] in the last quarter-verse.
And when a number is mentioned, the governing rule pertains to syllables.
The pratihārtṛ priest should recite the stobha interjections that are within the pratihāra,
and also those beyond that are separated by verse syllables.
In those whose last [portion] is an eight-syllable quarter-verse, [the pratihāra consists of] four [syllables], except in paṅkti [verses].
When unspecified, one should understand the end of the quarter-verse from the penultimate quarter-verse.

6.11.m: In the saumedha, the two aurṇāyava [sāmans], the pāvamāna ṛṣabha, and the mārgīyava having 'ī' as nidhana, the udgātṛ priest should recite the stobha interjection after the pratihāra.

In the iḍāsaṅkṣāra, the aśvasūkta, the aiḍasvara, the vārṣāhara, the svāra, the kautsa, the go-āṅgirasa sāman, the repetitive krauñca, and the agnimīyāma—which have the regular pratihāra—the pratihārtṛ priest [recites] before these.

6.11.s: shitamārṣabhśākalaṃ vājadāvaryaḥsvārsaimitraṃ padanidhane kāṇvarohitakūlīye yauktāśvasaubarṇṇānāmuttare yaudhājayannaudhasamāṣkāranidhanaṃ kāṇvaṃ yauktaśrucantiraścīnanidhanamāyāsyamindrasya yaśo vaiplavamuttarsaphaṃ pramhiṣṭhīyaṃ dīrghaṃ pauṣkalamāndhīgavaṃ vṛhadāgneyśyāvāśvatraiśoke teṣāṃ dve
6.11.d: स्हितमार्षभ्शाकलं वाजदावर्यःस्वार्सैमित्रं पदनिधने काण्वरोहितकूलीये यौक्ताश्वसौबर्ण्णानामुत्तरे यौधाजयन्नौधसमाष्कारनिधनं काण्वं यौक्तश्रुचन्तिरश्चीननिधनमायास्यमिन्द्रस्य यशो वैप्लवमुत्तर्सफं प्रम्हिष्ठीयं दीर्घं पौष्कलमान्धीगवं वृहदाग्नेय्श्यावाश्वत्रैशोके तेषां द्वे
6.11.m: In the sahitam, the ārṣabha-śākala, the vājadāvarī, the svāra, the saimitra, the two having a quarter-verse nidhana, the kāṇva-rohitakūlīya, the subsequent of the yauktāśva and saubarṇa [sāmans], the yaudhājaya, the naudhasa having the 'āṣ' syllable nidhana, the kāṇva, the yauktaśruca having a transverse nidhana, the āyāsya, the indrasya yaśas, the vaiplava, the uttarasapha, the prāmhiṣṭhīya, the dīrgha pauṣkala, the māndhīgava, the vṛhad-āgneya, the śyāvāśva, and the traiśoka: of these, [the pratihāra consists of] two [syllables].
In the former of the two yauktāśva [sāmans], the stobha interjection is in front.
In the śyāvāśva and traiśoka [sāmans], it is the end of the quarter-verse.
In the śyāvāśva, however, it is without stobha.
In the viśoviśīya [sāman], [the pratihāra] begins with the syllable om, with the third and fourth [syllables], prior to the hiṅkāra syllable.
Or it begins with the hiṅkāra syllable, with the fifth and sixth [syllables].

6.12.m: The śaukta and nārmedha [sāmans] have two pratihāras.
In the śaukta, [they are formed] by the first and ninth [syllables].
In the nārmedha, the former [pratihāra] is the end of the quarter-verse with four [syllables]; the subsequent [pratihāra] consists of the four middle [syllables].
Or it has a single pratihāra through the subsequent one.
In the two gāyatrī-sāmans, the bhāsa and the vairūpa, [the pratihāra is] the end of the quarter-verse with two [syllables] in the bhāsa, and with four [syllables] in the subsequent one.
In the sauhaviṣa having the yajñāyajñīya cadence, [it is formed] by the third quarter-verse.
In the śrāyantīya, the varuṇasāman, the dvaigata, and the añjas, [the pratihāra consists of] ten [syllables].

6.12.s: teṣāṃ pūrvayoḥ sarvaṃ padaṃ dve ca punaruktasya
6.12.d: तेषां पूर्वयोः सर्वं पदं द्वे च पुनरुक्तस्य
6.12.m: In the former two of these, it is an entire quarter-verse and two [syllables] of the repeated [part].
In the añjas, it is the beginning of the penultimate quarter-verse.
Or in the nine [sāmans] beginning with the viśoviśīya, [the pratihāra consists of] the first two [syllables] of the last quarter-verse.
In the viśoviśīya, it ends with the syllable 'hā-i'.
In the śrāyantīya and varuṇasāman, it begins with the repetition.

6.12.s: vāmadevy svārsākamaśvaṃ pāṣṭhauhannidhanakāmsatrāsāhīyaṃ kākṣīvataṃ cyāvanaṃ gāyatrīsāmauśanaṃ nidhanavadaidhmavāhaṃ teṣāṃ pañcamaṣaṣṭhe vikalpete nyāyyena vikalpete nyāyyena
6.12.d: वामदेव्य् स्वार्साकमश्वं पाष्ठौहन्निधनकाम्सत्रासाहीयं काक्षीवतं च्यावनं गायत्रीसामौशनं निधनवदैध्मवाहं तेषां पञ्चमषष्ठे विकल्पेते न्याय्येन विकल्पेते न्याय्येन
6.12.m: In the vāmadevya, the svāra, the sākamaśva, the pāṣṭhauha, the nidhanakāma, the satrāsāhīya, the kākṣīvata, the cyāvana, the gāyatrī-sāman, the auśana, and the aidhmavāha having a nidhana: the fifth and sixth [syllables] of these alternate with the regular [pratihāra]; they alternate with the regular [pratihāra].

7.1.s: gūrddaḥ saumedhaṃ mādhucchandasamaudalsauśravasamuttaraṃ vārtraturamṛṣabho raivataḥ kautsamauṣṇihamātīṣādīyaṃ krośamokonidhan svār sāmarājaṃ mārutamauṣṇihamākṣār sujñān hārivarṇ sāṃvarttañjāgataṃ varuṇasāmamarutāṃ dhenusraugmataṃ teṣāṃ catvāri
7.1.d: गूर्द्दः सौमेधं माधुच्छन्दसमौदल्सौश्रवसमुत्तरं वार्त्रतुरमृषभो रैवतः कौत्समौष्णिहमातीषादीयं क्रोशमोकोनिधन् स्वार् सामराजं मारुतमौष्णिहमाक्षार् सुज्ञान् हारिवर्ण् सांवर्त्तञ्जागतं वरुणसाममरुतां धेनुस्रौग्मतं तेषां चत्वारि
7.1.m: In the gūrda, the saumedha, the mādhucchandasa, the audala, the subsequent sauśravasa, the vārtratura, the raivata ṛṣabha, the kautsa, the auṣṇiha, the ātīṣādīya, the krośa, the svāra having the 'oko' nidhana, the sāmarāja, the māruta, the auṣṇiha, the ākṣāra, the sujñāna, the hārivarṇa, the sāṃvarta, the jāgata, the varuṇasāman, the dhenu of the Maruts, and the sraugmata: of these, [the pratihāra consists of] four [syllables].
In the following three, it begins with the repetition.
In the sauśravasa, [they are] the last ones, without stobhas.
In the ṛṣabha, it is the middle word.
In the following five, [they are] the middle ones.
In the kautsa, [they are] the last ones prior to the repetition.
Or in the sāmarāja, [they are] the first ones, along with the stobha in front.
Or six [syllables], beginning with the fifth, in the māruta [sāman].
Five in the āśva and rathantara [sāmans].
And in the vaidanvata [sāman] which contains repetition, the end of the pāda is in the last [part].
Or its first two [strophic verses] have stobhas on both sides.

7.2.s: ākūpārakrauñce gāyatrīsāmanī devātithaṃ gauṣūkt rauravaṃ dvihiṅkāraṃ vāmadevyamekārāntaprastāvaṃ vaiyaśvamaraṇye gey śākvaravarṇ saubharaṃ bārhadgirarāyo vājīye svāramaidhmavāhaṃ gauśṛṅg hārāyaṇaṃ kaulmalabarhiṣe janitramuttaraṃ vaitahavyamihavadvāmadevyaṃ pratīcīneḍaṅkāśītaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ pūrvśyaitsañjayaṃ teṣāṣaṭ
7.2.d: आकूपारक्रौञ्चे गायत्रीसामनी देवातिथं गौषूक्त् रौरवं द्विहिङ्कारं वामदेव्यमेकारान्तप्रस्तावं वैयश्वमरण्ये गेय् शाक्वरवर्ण् सौभरं बार्हद्गिररायो वाजीये स्वारमैध्मवाहं गौशृङ्ग् हारायणं कौल्मलबर्हिषे जनित्रमुत्तरं वैतहव्यमिहवद्वामदेव्यं प्रतीचीनेडङ्काशीतं वैष्णवं पूर्व्श्यैत्सञ्जयं तेषाषट्
7.2.m: The ākūpāra, krauñca, two gāyatrī sāmans, devātitha, gauṣūkta, raurava, dvihiṅkāra, vāmadevya with an e-ending prastāva, vaiyaśva to be sung in the forest, śākvaravarṇa, saubhara, bārhadgira, rāyovājīya, svāra aidhmavāha, gauśṛṅga, hārāyaṇa, the two kaulmalabarhiṣas, the subsequent janitra, vaitahavya, the vāmadevya with iha, the kāśīta with reversed iḍā, vaiṣṇava, and the former śyaita and sañjaya: of these, six [syllables are taken for the pratihāra].
In the first and third, [the pratihāras] have stobhas on both sides.
The first two strophic verses of the śākvaravarṇa have no pratihāra.
In the aidhmavāha, the stobha ends with the sound iha.
Before ovā in the three subsequent ones.
Or together with ovā in the paurumadga.
Or the end of the pāda [is taken] in the gauśṛṅga, hārāyaṇa, kaulmalabarhiṣa, and vaitahavya.
With two [syllables] in the former two, with four in the latter two.
The kaulmalabarhiṣa has an introductory stobha.

7.3.m: The kārṇaśravasa, traita, pajra, tauraśravasa, the subsequent śrudhya, udvaṃśaputra, and śākvara: of these, eight [syllables].
Half of them are at the end of the pāda in the pajra and tauraśravasa.
Of that [śrudhya], four upon gāyatrī verses.
Repetition of the middle pāda [takes place] in the śākvara.

7.3.s: vāyorabhikrandasvāraṅkāvamaurukṣayamauśanaśyāvāśve traiṣṭubhśnauṣṭaṃ jāgatsomasāma kārttayaśsvaraṃ payonidhanamṛṣabhaḥ śākvaro yaṇvāpatye teṣāmupottamaṃ padam
7.3.d: वायोरभिक्रन्दस्वारङ्कावमौरुक्षयमौशनश्यावाश्वे त्रैष्टुभ्श्नौष्टं जागत्सोमसाम कार्त्तयश्स्वरं पयोनिधनमृषभः शाक्वरो यण्वापत्ये तेषामुपोत्तमं पदम्
7.3.m: The vāyor abhikranda, svāra, kāva, aurukṣaya, auśana, śyāvāśva, traiṣṭubha, ānuṣṭubha, jāgata, somasāma, kārttayaśa, svara, payonidhana, ṛṣabha, śākvara, and the two yāṇvāpatyas: of these, the penultimate pāda [is the pratihāra].
The last three have introductory stobhas.
The first strophic verse of the two yāṇvāpatyas has no pratihāra.
Or four [syllables] of the five from the beginning in the last pāda.
The vaikhānasa, pauruhmanmana, udvaṃśīya, [the sāman] with the ā-kāra cadence, and the tvāṣṭrīsāma: of these, the last pāda before the repetition [is the pratihāra].
Or in the repetition, four [syllables] in the latter two [strophic verses].

7.4.s: śāktyasāma maidhātithaṃ vāravantīyamuttaramābhīśave simānāṃ niṣedhastriṇidhane tvāṣṭrīsāmāyāsyedārḍhacyutamātharvaṇaṃ revatya aiṭatamagnestriṇidhanamutsedhaniṣedhāvaiḍsākamaśvandairghaśravasandāsasyatyaṃ grāme geyaśyenastāni dvipratihārāṇi
7.4.d: शाक्त्यसाम मैधातिथं वारवन्तीयमुत्तरमाभीशवे सिमानां निषेधस्त्रिणिधने त्वाष्ट्रीसामायास्येदार्ढच्युतमाथर्वणं रेवत्य ऐटतमग्नेस्त्रिणिधनमुत्सेधनिषेधावैड्साकमश्वन्दैर्घश्रवसन्दासस्यत्यं ग्रामे गेयश्येनस्तानि द्विप्रतिहाराणि
7.4.m: The śāktyasāma, maidhātitha, subsequent vāravantīya, the two abhīśus, simānāṃ niṣedha, triṇidhana tvāṣṭrīsāma, āyāsya, dāḍhacyuta, ātharvaṇa, revatīs, aiṭa, the triṇidhana of Agni, utsedha-niṣedhas, aiḍa, sākamaśva, dairghaśravasa, dāśasyatya, and the śyena to be sung in the village: these have two pratihāras.
In the middle two pādas of the śāktyasāma and maidhātitha, the end of the pāda [is taken] with two or four [syllables].
In the vāravantīya, the two stobhas begin and end with the sound i.
Or [it has] a single pratihāra of seven [syllables] before the word ihāhā.
Or [the pratihāra] beginning with the sound u has the end of the pāda with one [syllable].

7.4.s: vāravantīyasya dvipadāsu saptānāsthāne catvāri dve caturṇām
7.4.d: वारवन्तीयस्य द्विपदासु सप्तानास्थाने चत्वारि द्वे चतुर्णाम्
7.4.m: In the dvipadā verses of the vāravantīya, four [syllables] take the place of seven, and two take the place of four.
[In the same way] two and one in an ekapadā verse.
In the latter two pādas of the subsequent [sāmans].
Two each, however, in the six beginning with the abhīśu.
Or four in the simānāṃ niṣedha.
The two [pratihāras] of the ātharvaṇa have introductory stobhas.
Four [syllables] in those beginning with it.
In the case of a single pratihāra, the former [pratihāra is combined] with the latter.
In the śyena, with the third and fifth pādas.
Or two syllables each in the fourth and sixth pādas.

7.5.m: The pratihāras of the santanin [sāman] are on separate strophic verses.
[There are] three each on the udder [verses] of the Mahānāmnī [verses].
Likewise the musical accents, and [three each] on the nityavatsā and atīṣaṅga [verses].
Or [there are] six on the last of the Śākvara [verses] among the Mahānāmnīs.
The middle staubhika word [is sung] on the purīṣa verses.
Some [teachers hold that] the inserted verses and purīṣa verses have no pratihāra.

7.5.s: tāsāṃ prathamadvitīye pade dvipadāstrīṇi śākvarāṇi dhāturvatsaūdhastacchākvaraṃ puruṣastrīṇi śākvarāṇyadhyāsyeti padāni
7.5.d: तासां प्रथमद्वितीये पदे द्विपदास्त्रीणि शाक्वराणि धातुर्वत्सऊधस्तच्छाक्वरं पुरुषस्त्रीणि शाक्वराण्यध्यास्येति पदानि
7.5.m: Their verses are: the first two are dvipadā verses; three are Śākvara verses; the calf of Dhātṛ, the udder, that Śākvara; Puruṣa; three Śākvara verses; and the inserted verse.

7.5.s: uttamā tu dvyadhyāsā dvipadāsu prastāvaḥ śākvaraprathameṣvadhyāsapurīṣeṣu ca
7.5.d: उत्तमा तु द्व्यध्यासा द्विपदासु प्रस्तावः शाक्वरप्रथमेष्वध्यासपुरीषेषु च
7.5.m: The last [verse], however, has two insertions; the prastāva is on the dvipadā verses, on the first Śākvara verses, and on the inserted and purīṣa verses.
By the bhāsa [sāman] the end of the verse has been stated; in the Vairūpa [sāman] it is on the Yajñāyajñīya deity-place.

7.5.s: araṇye geyaḥ śyenaḥ pārthuraśmamachidrarayiṣṭhe teṣāmuttareṣu padeṣu dve dve pūrvayoścatvāri catvāryuttarayoḥ
7.5.d: अरण्ये गेयः श्येनः पार्थुरश्ममछिद्ररयिष्ठे तेषामुत्तरेषु पदेषु द्वे द्वे पूर्वयोश्चत्वारि चत्वार्युत्तरयोः
7.5.m: The forest-sung [sāmans are]: Śyena, Pārthuraśma, Achidra, and Rayiṣṭha; on their subsequent verses [there are] two [pratihāras] each on the first two, and four each on the latter two.
The Pārthuraśma [sāman] has stobhas on both sides.
In the Vairūpa [sāman], the cadences are: 'deity-verse, deity-verse'.
Before the Śiśumatī [verse], the pratihāra is with stobhas.
In the Daivodāsa [sāman, the cadence] is the eleventh iḍā.
In the Traikakubha [sāman], one should repeat with the seventh and eighth [verses].
In the Vaiśvamanasa [sāman], with the ninth and tenth [verses].
Likewise in the Vṛṣan [sāman]; but with its three-times-uttered [verses].

7.5.s: sadṛśagītiṣu sarveṣu padeṣu pṛthakpadāni bhajeran pratyantādanādeśe śeṣamudgātā tāni vibhāgyāni
7.5.d: सदृशगीतिषु सर्वेषु पदेषु पृथक्पदानि भजेरन् प्रत्यन्तादनादेशे शेषमुद्गाता तानि विभाग्यानि
7.5.m: In all identical-singing verses, they should apportion the separate verses; where there is no specific instruction up to the ending part, the udgātṛ priest [sings] the rest; these are the apportionable [verses].

7.5.s: ādyantasrubdheṣu padāya padāya stobhedyoyaḥ padaṃ brūyāt
7.5.d: आद्यन्तस्रुब्धेषु पदाय पदाय स्तोभेद्योयः पदं ब्रूयात्
7.5.m: In [melodies] strung together at the beginning and the end, whoever speaks a verse should sing a stobha for verse after verse.

7.6.m: After the first verse, however, of the Saṃkṛti [sāman],
before the fourth verse, the pratihāra is with stobhas.

7.6.s: nidhanāni padānyupāyasadṛśāḥ stobhāntā yeṣāṃ tāni stobhavibhāgyāni
7.6.d: निधनानि पदान्युपायसदृशाः स्तोभान्ता येषां तानि स्तोभविभाग्यानि
7.6.m: Those whose verses are cadences, and whose endings are stobhas resembling the introductory passage (upāya), are apportionable by stobhas.
There, the pratihārtṛ priest should sing a stobha for the third verse only.
The stobhas of the Ekavṛṣa [sāman] have introductory passages (upāya).
And on the deities of the Śākvara Ṛṣabha [sāman].
For these, one should sing a stobha separately from the verses.

7.6.s: gāyatrīsāmasu vibhāgyeṣūttamaṃ vyāvarg śiṣṭvā pratiharediti dhānañjayyaḥ
7.6.d: गायत्रीसामसु विभाग्येषूत्तमं व्यावर्ग् शिष्ट्वा प्रतिहरेदिति धानञ्जय्यः
7.6.m: In apportionable Gāyatrī-sāmans, having left over the final section, he should make the pratihāra—so says Dhānañjayya.
With the entire verse—so says Śāṇḍilyāyana.
They should utter the thrice-uttered stobhas four times in the Śukriya [hymns], except for the cadences.
In the Mahādivākīrtya [sāman], one should transpose the two deities belonging to the prastāva.
Its body (ātman) is apportionable by stobhas.
The prastotṛ priest should sing the prastāva only for the first subordinate chant (anugāna) and for the body (ātman).
The other subordinate chants the udgātṛ priest alone should utter.
At their cadences, the two [other chanters] should join in with him.

7.6.s: uttamāni vā trīṇyanugānāni pratyāhṛtyetaraiḥ sahātmapadebhyaḥ stobhadharmeṇānusaṃhareyuḥ
7.6.d: उत्तमानि वा त्रीण्यनुगानानि प्रत्याहृत्येतरैः सहात्मपदेभ्यः स्तोभधर्मेणानुसंहरेयुः
7.6.m: Or, having brought back the last three subordinate chants together with the others, they should conclude after the body verses according to the rule of stobhas.
Those which are before the body [are sung] once at the beginning of the stotra; those which are after, once at the end of the stotra.
Or [they are sung] at the beginning and end of each round (paryāya).
In the bhāsa-cadence, the udgātṛ priest alone should utter the introductory passage of the tenth verse.
In the Rājana [sāman], they should utter all the thrice-uttered [words] five times.
Its stobhas are verse by verse; the prastāva is with a verse.
The pratihāra is with the third verse preceded by a stobha.

7.6.s: tatra devatābhyo yadyadanantaraṃ pūrvaṃ padantena sahainā brūyuḥ
7.6.d: तत्र देवताभ्यो यद्यदनन्तरं पूर्वं पदन्तेन सहैना ब्रूयुः
7.6.m: There, with whichever verse is immediately prior to the deities, together with that [verse] they should utter them.
One should interpose a stobha between the verse and the deity—so say some.

7.7.m: In the verse-stobhas, the verses are cadences; likewise the iḍās.
The prastotṛ priest [sings stobhas] for the first three.
The pratihārtṛ priest [sings] only for the three beginning with the seventh.
The cadence is half a verse when separated by an iḍā.
The first quarter-verse of the fourth [verse consists of] four three-syllable cadences.
Or the second and last [are cadences]; and the other two are twofold, four syllables each.

[The pratihāra is made] with the eighth stobha interjections in the case of the first [verse], with the ninth in the case of the middle two, [and] with the tenth in the case of the last, or else with the ninth.
In the last following chant of the Ilānda [sāman], there are six.
Or the first is divisible;
there [it is made] with the middle word of the last stobha interjection.
Eleven in the case of the [sāman] of Dīrghatamas.
[The pratihāra is made] with the eighth stobha interjections in the Bhadra and Śreyas [sāmans],
and with the fifth if there are two pratihāras.
In the Dharma and Vidharma [sāmans], the stobha interjection being divisible by groups of five syllables,
in those two, the pratihāra is made with the tenth stobha interjection,
and with the sixth if there are two pratihāras.
In the Sauhaviṣa [sāman], [there are] three [syllables] at the end of the pāda,
In the Sauhaviṣa, the middle word having a musical accent is in the cadence;
In the Vairāja [sāman], only the middle word, preceded by the stobha interjection, [is the pratihāra].
Its pāda-ends should be repeated four times, or three times.
Likewise [in the sāman] of Vatsapri belonging to the fourth day.

7.7.s: avibhāgyānāmuttame pade prāgupāyāt ṣaṭsu vyāvargavatsvaṣṭasu vā yathā vāmadevyakrośe pūrveṇa vyāvargeṇa pratiharediti dhānañjayyaḥ
7.7.d: अविभाग्यानामुत्तमे पदे प्रागुपायात् षट्सु व्यावर्गवत्स्वष्टसु वा यथा वामदेव्यक्रोशे पूर्वेण व्यावर्गेण प्रतिहरेदिति धानञ्जय्यः
7.7.m: In the case of indivisible [chants], in the last pāda before the upāya, when there are six or eight [syllables] possessing a pause, as in the Vāmadevyakrośa, one should make the pratihāra with the earlier pause—thus says Dhānañjayya.
With the subsequent one—thus says Śāṇḍilyāyana.
The pratihāra-section chant alone is the pratihāra, even if not at the beginning of a pāda, in [verses] of different meters.
After the pratihāra, one should not begin with the syllable Om—thus says Dhānañjayya.

7.8.m: However, in the case of vowels that are modulated downwards, one should take up [the chant] directly.

7.8.s: yathā kāleyasya nakā33333riṇām yathā vātsasya mayo3333vā3
7.8.d: यथा कालेयस्य नका33333रिणाम् यथा वात्सस्य मयो3333वा3
7.8.m: As nakā33333riṇām of the Kāleya [sāman], as mayo3333vā3 of the Vātsa [sāman].
In the case of vowels that are modulated downwards, one should begin with the syllable Om—thus says Gautama.

7.8.s: ihakāraiḍāthakārau gītañca nidhanasvarhīṣīsvarañca dvyakṣaraṃ devatāścāraṇye geyeṣu tānyantaḥsāmanidhanāni vāk cet stobhānto'nantaraḥ purastāt vṛddhaḥ kṛṣṭo vā kāraḥ svaritaṃ vārcikaṃ vā vṛddhaṃ pūrveṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ yathā revatyastvāṣṭrīsāma yaudhājayaṃ dārḍhacyutamātharvaṇamāndhīgavamihavadvāmadevyam
7.8.d: इहकारैडाथकारौ गीतञ्च निधनस्वर्हीषीस्वरञ्च द्व्यक्षरं देवताश्चारण्ये गेयेषु तान्यन्तःसामनिधनानि वाक् चेत् स्तोभान्तोऽनन्तरः पुरस्तात् वृद्धः कृष्टो वा कारः स्वरितं वार्चिकं वा वृद्धं पूर्वेषां त्रयाणां यथा रेवत्यस्त्वाष्ट्रीसाम यौधाजयं दार्ढच्युतमाथर्वणमान्धीगवमिहवद्वामदेव्यम्
7.8.m: The sounds iha and iḍā and tha, and the melody, and that which has the tone of a cadence, and the two-syllable hīṣī tone, and deities in the forest-sung melodies: these are interior cadences of the sāman, if there is a word [following], an immediately following stobha-ending preceded by a lengthened or drawn-out syllable, or a circumflex, or a metric lengthened [vowel] of the first three; as the Revatīs, the Tvāṣṭrī-sāman, the Yaudhājaya, the Dārḍhacyuta, the Ātharvaṇa, the Āndhīgava, and the Ihavat-vāmadevya.
Together with that which immediately follows upon them in the manner of recited text, belonging to the ṛc, they should join in, unless specified otherwise.
In the Purīṣa hymns, the metric [portion is taken] from the prastāva.
In the Ihavat-vāmadevya, [it is] the subsequent two iha sounds.
In the three-cadence Tvāṣṭrī-sāman, [it begins with] the upagraha and following.
In the third following chant of the Ilānda [sāman], there is an option regarding the sound iha.
And in the Ātīṣādīya, in the middle cadence.
In the Paurumīḍha, there is no middle cadence.
And in the Āṣṭādaṣṭra, Sadoviśīya, and Arkapuṣpa [sāmans].
They should all join in upon the iḍā beginning with the vowel i; those are the rearward iḍās.
Others [should join in upon that] ending in the vowel u—thus says Gautama.

7.8.s: ikārāntañcaivopāy saṃpragāyanti kutsā evaṃ naḥ kṛtsneḍopetā bhaviṣyatīti pratyudgītastu khalveṣāṃ tathodgātā bhavati
7.8.d: इकारान्तञ्चैवोपाय् संप्रगायन्ति कुत्सा एवं नः कृत्स्नेडोपेता भविष्यतीति प्रत्युद्गीतस्तु खल्वेषां तथोद्गाता भवति
7.8.m: And the Kutsas join in chanting ending with the vowel i on the upāya, [saying,] 'Thus our entire iḍā will be joined'; however, their udgātṛ priest chants in response accordingly.

7.9.m: In pragātha verses, in the case of the Bṛhat and Rathantara [sāmans] and of the Yajñāyajñīya, when not specifically stated, the subsequent two [verses] are kakubh verses.
In both of them, the prastāva consists of two syllables everywhere.
In triplets, however, through the joining of syllables,
the last syllable of the first [verse] and the first of the middle [verse are joined];
in this very same manner, the latter two of the second and last [verses].
In [verses] of different meters, when not specifically stated, one should seek everywhere to make the syllable measure of the prastāva, pratihāra, and cadences conform to the prototype.

7.9.s: pāṅktasyānuṣṭupsu dvitīyaṃ padaṃ dvaidhaṃ vyūhedyatharṣabhasya śākvarasya caturakṣaraśaḥ
7.9.d: पाङ्क्तस्यानुष्टुप्सु द्वितीयं पदं द्वैधं व्यूहेद्यथर्षभस्य शाक्वरस्य चतुरक्षरशः
7.9.m: When a pāṅkta sāman is on anuṣṭubh verses, one should divide the second pāda in two, as in the Ṛṣabha and Śākvara [sāmans], by four syllables each.
The third [pāda], as in the Sāṅkṛtina [sāman] on bṛhatī verses, into eight syllables and four syllables.

7.9.s: yonau yānyabhyāsenānyachandaḥ sampadyate yathā gaurīvitaudale kautsaṃ traikakubhavaikhānase tadāpanneṣu gautamasārdāgavāvanabhyāsam
7.9.d: योनौ यान्यभ्यासेनान्यछन्दः सम्पद्यते यथा गौरीवितौदले कौत्सं त्रैककुभवैखानसे तदापन्नेषु गौतमसार्दागवावनभ्यासम्
7.9.m: In the prototype, those which become another meter through repetition, as the Gaurīvita on Audala verses, the Kautsa on Traikakubha and Vaikhānasa verses: when they have attained that [meter], Gautama and Sārdāgava [prescribe] no repetition.
Maśaka Gārgya [prescribes] repetition; Maśaka Gārgya [prescribes] repetition.

7.10.m: In the Upāsthāna chants, there are other cadences.
When no tone is specified, they should have the same tone [as the base chant].
The sesquialteral [iḍā] belongs to the sesquialteral Upasthāna chants.
And in the Daivodāsa and Sujñāna [sāmans].
"the latter [has it]," say Gautama and Dhānañjayya.
In the two Aupagava [sāmans], "atha" or "mathā" [is the cadence];
"optional, but in malevolent rites it is 'nānā', or 'mathā', and 'atha' elsewhere."

8.1.m: When there is no specific instruction, the time for sacrifice is at the concurrence of the northern course of the sun, the bright fortnight, and an auspicious day.
And when only a number is specified, the sacrificial gifts are cows.
By “gold” one should understand natural gold.
For one-day sacrifices, one should undergo consecration on the first day of the bright fortnight.
Or having observed the conjunction of the asterism.
When there is no specific instruction, their consecration is for one day, or three, four, or an unlimited number.

8.1.s: jyotiṣṭomasyokthānāmuttare saubharanārmedha atirātra ukthānta itarāṇīti gautamo vṛttigrahaṇāt
8.1.d: ज्योतिष्टोमस्योक्थानामुत्तरे सौभरनार्मेध अतिरात्र उक्थान्त इतराणीति गौतमो वृत्तिग्रहणात्
8.1.m: Of the Uktha lauds of the Jyotiṣṭoma, the Saubhara and the Nārmedha are [employed] on the latter ones; Gautama says that these two are in an Atirātra, while the others conclude with an Uktha laud, on account of the use of the term vṛtti.
Dhānañjayya says there is no fixed rule for the others, because the traditional recitation makes no distinction.
Śāṇḍilya says that the others too are in an Atirātra, on account of the equal injunction.
There should be an option between the two Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra chants.
Authorities who take the Saubhara and the Nārmedha as standard consider the optional Uktha-metre connections to belong to the Atirātra.
The use of the anuṣṭubh verses, however, is found through the night ritual procedure.
And the Nārmedha is seen elsewhere than in the night ritual procedure, as in the five-day period of the Abhiplava.
Its strophic verse should be in the anuṣṭubh metre, or it may have a different metre in sacrifices concluding with an Uktha laud, on account of the division of usage in Atirātras.
The optional forms of the independent Jyotiṣṭoma are the Agniṣṭoma, the Ukthya, and the Atirātra.
For that [sacrifice] when not an Atirātra, the sacrificial gifts are one hundred and twelve [cows].

8.1.s: viśvajidabhijitaṃ yamābhyāṃ yajamānaḥ pūrvāparābhyāṃ yajeteti dhānañjayyaḥ
8.1.d: विश्वजिदभिजितं यमाभ्यां यजमानः पूर्वापराभ्यां यजेतेति धानञ्जय्यः

8.1.m: The sacrificial ground of the Abhijit should be to the south, and that of the Viśvajit to the north.
Opposite them should be the wife’s hall.
The officiating priests are separate, and whatever rite is inside the altar ground [is separate].
Now, whatever is outside the altar ground is common.

8.1.s: abhijitaḥ pūvaṃ pūrvaṃ karma santiṣṭheta viśvajita uttaram
8.1.d: अभिजितः पूवं पूर्वं कर्म सन्तिष्ठेत विश्वजित उत्तरम्
8.1.m: The ritual act of the Abhijit should conclude earlier, [and that] of the Viśvajit later.
For both of them, the sacrificial gifts [consist] separately of a thousand [cows].
However, one who has a specific desire may sacrifice with these two.
The sacrificial gifts for the Abhijit are a thousand [cows]; for the Viśvajit, either a hundred horses, a thousand [cows], or one's entire property.

8.2.s: tasyāvabhṛthādudetya rohiṇīṃ vatsacchvīṃ paridhāya dharmān kuryyātta uktā brāhmaṇena
8.2.d: तस्यावभृथादुदेत्य रोहिणीं वत्सच्छ्वीं परिधाय धर्मान् कुर्य्यात्त उक्ता ब्राह्मणेन
8.2.m: Having emerged from its concluding purificatory bath [and] put on the red hide of a calf, he should perform the observances; they have been stated by the Brāhmaṇa.
As for '[He] stays three nights in the forest,' he should dwell near an udumbara tree.
Even in the absence of an udumbara tree, they should dig in a branch of an udumbara tree.

8.2.s: khanitreṇa jīvatīti yattatra khāny syāttena jīvet
8.2.d: खनित्रेण जीवतीति यत्तत्र खान्य् स्यात्तेन जीवेत्
8.2.m: As for 'He lives by a digging tool,' he should live on whatever edible roots may be found there.
In the absence of edible roots, having buried grain vessels, he should live by digging them up.
As for 'The spade is sharpened at both ends,' it is made of bamboo [and is] variegated, says Śāṇḍilya.
Whatever [spade it may be], says Dhānañjayya.

8.2.s: niṣādeṣu tisro vasatīti pārśvato niṣādagrāmasya vaset
8.2.d: निषादेषु तिस्रो वसतीति पार्श्वतो निषादग्रामस्य वसेत्
8.2.m: As for '[He] stays three nights among the Niṣādas,' he should dwell beside a village of Niṣādas.

8.2.s: teṣāṃ kāmamāraṇyaṃ bhuñjīta naivār śyāmākaṃ mārgamiti
8.2.d: तेषां काममारण्यं भुञ्जीत नैवार् श्यामाकं मार्गमिति
8.2.m: At will, he may consume their forest food, [namely] wild rice, millet, [and] game.

8.2.s: jane tisro vasatīti rājanyabandhurjano brāhmaṇaḥ samānajana iti śāṇḍilyaḥ
8.2.d: जने तिस्रो वसतीति राजन्यबन्धुर्जनो ब्राह्मणः समानजन इति शाण्डिल्यः
8.2.m: As for '[He] stays three nights among the people,' 'people' means an unanointed kṣatriya, [and] 'one's own people' means a brāhmaṇa, says Śāṇḍilya.

8.2.s: vivāhyo janaḥ sagotraḥ samānajana iti dhānañjayyaḥ
8.2.d: विवाह्यो जनः सगोत्रः समानजन इति धानञ्जय्यः
8.2.m: 'People' means those with whom marriage is possible; 'one's own people' means those of the same gotra, says Dhānañjayya.

8.2.s: prativeśo janapado jano yatra vaset sa samānajana iti śāṇḍilyāyanaḥ
8.2.d: प्रतिवेशो जनपदो जनो यत्र वसेत् स समानजन इति शाण्डिल्यायनः
8.2.m: 'People' means a neighbouring country; wherever he resides, that is 'one's own people', says Śāṇḍilyāyana.
These observances belong to all [sacrifices] in which the sacrificial gift is one's entire property.
In all rites containing the Mahāvrata, having taken the consecration on a new-moon day, he should bind the ukhā pot, except in the case of year-long rites, says Gautama.
Having added six days along with the soma-pressing days beyond the year, they should rise [from the session].

8.2.s: samāpte vā saṃvatsare rātrisatreṣu rājānaṃ krīṇīyuḥ
8.2.d: समाप्ते वा संवत्सरे रात्रिसत्रेषु राजानं क्रीणीयुः

8.2.m: However, they should take the consecration in the first fortnight according to their social class.
Or everywhere according to social class, if the initiation [into Vedic study] has taken place elsewhere, says Dhānañjayya.
Even if uninitiated, says Śāṇḍilya.
There are three upasads for the one-day Mahāvrata rite, according to Gautama's view,
There he should give a chariot drawn by horses and a hundred [cows] to the brahman priest;
likewise to the adhvaryu priest who piles the fire-altar;
and to the udgātṛ priest chanting with the pṛṣṭha laud;
or the sacrificial gift is one's entire property.
All thousand-[gift] sacrifices have a thousand as sacrificial gift separately.

8.3.s: sādyaḥkreṇa yakṣyamāṇo mahārātreḥ prātarāhuti hutvācakṣītartvigbhyaḥ sādyaḥkroma iti
8.3.d: साद्यःक्रेण यक्ष्यमाणो महारात्रेः प्रातराहुति हुत्वाचक्षीतर्त्विग्भ्यः साद्यःक्रोम इति
8.3.m: One intending to sacrifice with a Sādyaḥkra rite, having offered the morning oblation in the late night, should declare to the officiating priests: 'A Sādyaḥkra rite for us.'

8.3.s: praga eva prahiṇuyāditi dhānañjayyo dīkṣāprabhṛti sadyaḥ sarvaṃ kuryyuḥ prathamadvitīyayoḥ śyenasya ca
8.3.d: प्रग एव प्रहिणुयादिति धानञ्जय्यो दीक्षाप्रभृति सद्यः सर्वं कुर्य्युः प्रथमद्वितीययोः श्येनस्य च
8.3.m: He should send [word] early in the morning, says Dhānañjayya; beginning with the consecration, they should perform everything in a single day for the first and second [Sādyaḥkra] and for the Śyena sacrifice.
There are six Sādyaḥkra rites ending with the Ekatrika, says Śaucivṛkṣi.

8.3.s: urvarā vediriti prathame yavorvarā pakkā syādvrīhyurvarā vā
8.3.d: उर्वरा वेदिरिति प्रथमे यवोर्वरा पक्का स्याद्व्रीह्युर्वरा वा
8.3.m: As for 'The altar is a cultivated field,' in the first [Sādyaḥkra] it should be a field of ripe barley or a field of ripe rice.

8.3.s: tata eva samutkarttaṃ khala uttaravediṃ kuryyuḥ
8.3.d: तत एव समुत्कर्त्तं खल उत्तरवेदिं कुर्य्युः
8.3.m: Right from there, having cut around, they should make the high altar on a threshing floor.

8.3.s: khalevālī yūpo bhavatīti lāṅgaleṣā yūpaḥ syāt kalāpī caṣālabhāgā
8.3.d: खलेवाली यूपो भवतीति लाङ्गलेषा यूपः स्यात् कलापी चषालभागा
8.3.m: As for 'The post in the threshing floor becomes the sacrificial post,' the shaft of a plow should be the sacrificial post, and a bunch [of stalks] serves as the top-ring.
If he should sacrifice when the barley season or the rice season has passed, having sown grain vessels, they should plow around.
The grain vessels should be the high altar, and a basket serves as the top-ring.

8.3.s: trivatsaḥ sāṇḍa iti bahutrivarṣasya jānapadī trivatsa iti
8.3.d: त्रिवत्सः साण्ड इति बहुत्रिवर्षस्य जानपदी त्रिवत्स इति
8.3.m: As for 'A three-year-old uncastrated bull,' 'trivatsa' is a regional word for a well-grown three-year-old [animal];

8.3.s: prāñchotāraṃ baheyurudañcamudgātāraṃ pratyañcamadhvaryyuṃ dakṣiṇā brahmāṇaṃ purastādvātra vaseyustatraibhyaḥ somaṃ prabrūyuraśvarathairyātvā na uktā brāhmaṇenādhvānaśca
8.3.d: प्राञ्छोतारं बहेयुरुदञ्चमुद्गातारं प्रत्यञ्चमध्वर्य्युं दक्षिणा ब्रह्माणं पुरस्ताद्वात्र वसेयुस्तत्रैभ्यः सोमं प्रब्रूयुरश्वरथैर्यात्वा न उक्ता ब्राह्मणेनाध्वानश्च
8.3.m: They should convey the hotṛ priest to the east, the udgātṛ priest to the north, the adhvaryu priest to the west, the brahman priest to the south; or they should reside beforehand at that place; having traveled with horse chariots, they should announce King Soma to them there; and the distances have been stated by the Brāhmaṇa.

8.3.s: kuryyurevartvija iti śāṇḍilyo'nyāsu brāhmaṇāstānadhvana ūḍhvā tatraibhyaḥ somaṃ pravrūyurasau sadyaḥ kriyā yajate tadahaṃ pravravīmīndrāya viśvebhyo devebhyo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ somyebhyaḥ somapebhya iti
8.3.d: कुर्य्युरेवर्त्विज इति शाण्डिल्योऽन्यासु ब्राह्मणास्तानध्वन ऊढ्वा तत्रैभ्यः सोमं प्रव्रूयुरसौ सद्यः क्रिया यजते तदहं प्रव्रवीमीन्द्राय विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सोम्येभ्यः सोमपेभ्य इति
8.3.m: The officiating priests themselves should perform [it], says Śāṇḍilya; [or] in other [traditions] brāhmaṇas, having conveyed them over those distances, should announce King Soma to them there: 'So-and-so sacrifices with a single-day rite; that I announce to Indra, to the All-Gods, to the soma-worthy, soma-drinking brāhmaṇas.'

8.3.s: sa kṣīradṛtayorathā bhavantīti sadyo dugdhena kṣīreṇa dṛtayaḥ pūrṇāḥ syustato'yannavanītamudīyāt pheno vā tadājye'pi sṛjeyuḥ
8.3.d: स क्षीरदृतयोरथा भवन्तीति सद्यो दुग्धेन क्षीरेण दृतयः पूर्णाः स्युस्ततोऽयन्नवनीतमुदीयात् फेनो वा तदाज्येऽपि सृजेयुः
8.3.m: As for 'Those chariots have milk-skins,' skins should be filled with freshly milked milk; whatever butter or foam rises from that, they should mix that into the clarified butter.

8.3.s: aśvaḥ śveta etasya dakṣiṇā tamudgātre dadyāt kiñciccetarebhyaḥ
8.3.d: अश्वः श्वेत एतस्य दक्षिणा तमुद्गात्रे दद्यात् किञ्चिच्चेतरेभ्यः
8.3.m: A white horse is the sacrificial gift for this [rite]; he should give it to the udgātṛ priest, and something to the others.

8.4.m: By this very [explanation] the subsequent [rite] is explained.
And of that [rite], a horse is the twenty-first among the sacrificial gifts, or just beyond that.

8.4.s: ekarātrīṇo dvyahīno'nukrīste'ṅgirasa ādityebhyaḥ śvaḥ sutyāmiti hyāha
8.4.d: एकरात्रीणो द्व्यहीनोऽनुक्रीस्तेऽङ्गिरस आदित्येभ्यः श्वः सुत्यामिति ह्याह
8.4.m: The Anukrī is a two-day sacrifice performed in a single night, for [the Brāhmaṇa] says: 'The Aṅgirases [announced] to the Ādityas: "Tomorrow is the soma-pressing day!"'

8.4.s: tasya krayaprabhṛtyuttamahaḥ syāditi gautamastsadyaḥ parikrīyeti hyādityānāha netarān
8.4.d: तस्य क्रयप्रभृत्युत्तमहः स्यादिति गौतमस्त्सद्यः परिक्रीयेति ह्यादित्यानाह नेतरान्
8.4.m: Its final day should begin with the purchase [of soma], says Gautama, for [the Brāhmaṇa] says: 'Having bought around in a single day' to the Ādityas, not to the others;
and the name 'Anukrī' [arises] from purchasing on the following day.

8.4.s: upavasathāntaṃ pūrvamahaḥ syāditi dhānañjayyaḥ śvaḥsutyāmiti hyāheti śvaḥ krayaṃ prābruvannityabhaviṣyat
8.4.d: उपवसथान्तं पूर्वमहः स्यादिति धानञ्जय्यः श्वःसुत्यामिति ह्याहेति श्वः क्रयं प्राब्रुवन्नित्यभविष्यत्
8.4.m: The earlier day should end with the day of preparation, says Dhānañjayya; for [the Brāhmaṇa] says: 'Tomorrow is the soma-pressing day'; if they had said 'tomorrow is the purchase,' it would be [as Gautama says];

8.4.s: t sadyaḥ parikrīyeti ca prathamasya sadyastāṃ darśayati
8.4.d: त् सद्यः परिक्रीयेति च प्रथमस्य सद्यस्तां दर्शयति
8.4.m: and 'Having bought around in a single day' indicates the single-day nature of the first [day].
Because it is a two-day ahīna, however, the Aṅgirases bought [soma] on the later day; therefore its name is 'Anukrī'.
A horse is the one hundred and first among its sacrificial gifts, or [it is] just a horse.
By this the Viśvajicchilpa is explained.
It is a three-day ahīna lasting two nights, according to Śāṇḍilya.
The first day pertains to consecration, beginning with the soma-purchase and ending with the upavasatha day; the second, highest [day] pertains to the soma-pressing.

8.4.s: tasya dakṣiṇā yānāni yathotsāhaṃ dadyāttasmin janapade yānyabhidhyātatamāni syuḥ
8.4.d: तस्य दक्षिणा यानानि यथोत्साहं दद्यात्तस्मिन् जनपदे यान्यभिध्याततमानि स्युः
8.4.m: As sacrificial gifts for it, he should give vehicles according to his ability, whichever are most coveted in that country.

8.4.s: sarvavedasanirmāndadyāditi dhānañjayyo vimit śayanamārohaṇamahānase dāsamithunau dhānyapaly sīraṃ dhenuriti dhenuriti
8.4.d: सर्ववेदसनिर्मान्दद्यादिति धानञ्जय्यो विमित् शयनमारोहणमहानसे दासमिथुनौ धान्यपल्य् सीरं धेनुरिति धेनुरिति
