8.4.m: He should give all his property minus the measures [of household necessities], according to Dhānañjayya: a hut, a bed, a mounting-step, two kitchen slaves, a grain-winnowing basket, a plow, and a milch cow—a milch cow.

8.5.m: For the Śyena rite, he should choose as officiating priests learned sons of warrior troops.
Only of worthy [brāhmaṇas], according to Śāṇḍilya.
He should churn the clarified butter from those [cows] that are unaffected among cows struck by the wind.

8.5.s: yatra stambā vṛkṣā vā bahulā jātāḥ syustāśchedan devayajanaṃ kuryuḥ
8.5.d: यत्र स्तम्बा वृक्षा वा बहुला जाताः स्युस्ताश्छेदन् देवयजनं कुर्युः
8.5.m: Where dense clumps of reeds or trees have grown, they should clear them and make the sacrificial ground.
Or a barren, parched bare ground.

8.5.s: śavanabhye adhiṣavaṇe iti yena yānena mṛtaṃ nirvaheyustasya nabhye adhiṣavaṇaphalake kuryuḥ
8.5.d: शवनभ्ये अधिषवणे इति येन यानेन मृतं निर्वहेयुस्तस्य नभ्ये अधिषवणफलके कुर्युः
8.5.m: Regarding the rule, "The two pressing-boards are the two hubs of a funeral cart": they should make the two pressing-boards out of the two hubs of the vehicle in which they convey a corpse.
The sacrificial post is without a top-ring and has the tip of a wooden sword.

8.5.s: lohitoṣṇīṣā lohitavāsaso nivītā ṛtvijaḥ pracareyurupotaparuṣā ujyadhanvānaḥ
8.5.d: लोहितोष्णीषा लोहितवाससो निवीता ऋत्विजः प्रचरेयुरुपोतपरुषा उज्यधन्वानः
8.5.m: The officiating priests should officiate wearing red turbans, red garments, with their sacred threads hung straight down over the neck, dressed in bristly skins, holding unstrung bows.

8.5.s: pavamāne rathantaraṃ karotīti bṛhatyāmekarcānāsthāne syādekaṃ taddhi bārhatānā sthānamevañca tṛce bhavati
8.5.d: पवमाने रथन्तरं करोतीति बृहत्यामेकर्चानास्थाने स्यादेकं तद्धि बार्हताना स्थानमेवञ्च तृचे भवति
8.5.m: Regarding the rule, "He performs the Rathantara in the pavamāna chant": it should take the place of a single verse in a Bṛhatī verse; for that is the single place of verses composed in the Bṛhatī meter, and thus it occurs in a triplet.
"He should adapt it without conflict with the others" is another view; thus the modification is smaller.

8.5.s: tatra pañcamaṃ vārhatamāharet stomavaśena tat paurumadg syāt bhrātṛvyavadh hyasmin brāhmaṇaṃ darśayati
8.5.d: तत्र पञ्चमं वार्हतमाहरेत् स्तोमवशेन तत् पौरुमद्ग् स्यात् भ्रातृव्यवध् ह्यस्मिन् ब्राह्मणं दर्शयति
8.5.m: There he should introduce a fifth verse in the Bṛhatī meter according to the requirement of the stoma; that should be the Paurumadga, for the Brāhmaṇa indicates the slaying of the rival in connection with this.

8.5.s: pṛṣṭheṣu rathantarasyottarayordvipade syātāmityācāryā evaṃ suparācyo bhavantīti
8.5.d: पृष्ठेषु रथन्तरस्योत्तरयोर्द्विपदे स्यातामित्याचार्या एवं सुपराच्यो भवन्तीति
8.5.m: In the pṛṣṭha lauds, the two subsequent verses of the Rathantara should be two-footed verses, according to the teachers, so that they are facing away in this manner.
They should be two Kakubh verses, according to Gautama, because this indicates non-repetition of the stoma.
When making the Plava into the brahma-sāman, he should perform it on the verses of the Śyaita.

8.5.s: nava nava dakṣiṇā iti navavargānyathotsāhaṃ dadyāt kāṇakhorakūṭabaṇḍānām
8.5.d: नव नव दक्षिणा इति नववर्गान्यथोत्साहं दद्यात् काणखोरकूटबण्डानाम्
8.5.m: Regarding the rule, "Sacrificial gifts in groups of nine, nine": he should give groups of nine according to his ability, consisting of one-eyed, lame, hornless, and docked animals.
They should also draw blood from them at the time of giving the sacrificial gifts.
In the Ekatrika rite, they should perform everything in a single day.
It has one consecration day and three upasads, according to Gautama.
Its third pressing has the Gāyatrapārśva sāman on the verse beginning "ayā rucā".

8.5.s: purojityāmiti śāṇḍilyastasyāḥ sa sunve yo vasūnāmityetāṃ madhye kuryāt
8.5.d: पुरोजित्यामिति शाण्डिल्यस्तस्याः स सुन्वे यो वसूनामित्येतां मध्ये कुर्यात्
8.5.m: It is on the verse beginning "purojitī", according to Śāṇḍilya; in the middle of it he should insert the verse beginning "sa sunve yo vasūnām".

8.5.s: prācīmanu pradiśaṃ yāti cekitadityetasyāmudvśīyaṃ kuryāduddhṛtya gāyatrapārśvamiti lāmakāyanaḥ
8.5.d: प्राचीमनु प्रदिशं याति चेकितदित्येतस्यामुद्व्शीयं कुर्यादुद्धृत्य गायत्रपार्श्वमिति लामकायनः
8.5.m: Having removed the Gāyatrapārśva, he should perform the Udvamśīya on the verse beginning "prācīmanu pradiśaṃ yāti cekitat", according to Lāmakāyana.

8.5.s: trikaṃ vahiṣpavamān syāditi dhānañjayyaḥ pañcī madhyandinaḥ saptyārbhava ekīnītarāṇīti
8.5.d: त्रिकं वहिष्पवमान् स्यादिति धानञ्जय्यः पञ्ची मध्यन्दिनः सप्त्यार्भव एकीनीतराणीति
8.5.m: The bahiṣpavamāna chant should be a three-verse stoma; the midday pressing should be a five-verse stoma; the third pressing should be a seven-verse stoma; the others should be one-verse stomas, according to Dhānañjayya.
The pavamāna chants and the hotṛ's sāmans are three-verse stomas, and the others are one-verse stomas.
Constituted with increments of four, two by two, descending in groups of three and five.
Its sacrificial gifts are one hundred and sixty-six.

8.6.s: vrātyastomairyakṣyamāṇāḥ pṛthagagnīnādhāya yajñopakaraṇāni ceṣṭvā ya eṣāmadhyayane'bhikrāntitamaḥ syādabhijanena vā tadabhāve'pi bhogalābhena tasya gārhapate dīkṣeran bhakṣāścānu bhakṣayeyuḥ
8.6.d: व्रात्यस्तोमैर्यक्ष्यमाणाः पृथगग्नीनाधाय यज्ञोपकरणानि चेष्ट्वा य एषामध्ययनेऽभिक्रान्तितमः स्यादभिजनेन वा तदभावेऽपि भोगलाभेन तस्य गार्हपते दीक्षेरन् भक्षाश्चानु भक्षयेयुः
8.6.m: Those who intend to sacrifice with the vrātyastoma sacrifices, having separately set up their sacred fires and performed the preliminary sacrificial preparations, should undergo consecration at the gārhapatya fire of the one among them who is most distinguished in learning or by descent, or in the absence of that, by the acquisition of wealth; and they should consume the portions after him.

8.6.s: ye ke ca vrātyāḥ sampādayeyuste prathamena yajeran
8.6.d: ये के च व्रात्याः सम्पादयेयुस्ते प्रथमेन यजेरन्
8.6.m: Whichever vrātyas assemble together, they should sacrifice with the first [vrātyastoma].
Those who are deprived of generative power due to old age are the 'śamanīcāmeḍhra' [men of extinguished or lowered virility].

8.6.s: yanniruktaṃ nidhanamupeyuritīndreti dyautāne nidhanaṃ nirāhustasya pratiṣedhaḥ
8.6.d: यन्निरुक्तं निधनमुपेयुरितीन्द्रेति द्यौताने निधनं निराहुस्तस्य प्रतिषेधः
8.6.m: Regarding the rule, "They should not adopt a formulated cadence": they explicitly pronounce the cadence as "Indra" in the Dyautāna sāman; this is a prohibition of that.
Regarding the rule, "A turban and a goad": the turban is that which is tied across by the vrātyas.

8.6.s: dhanuṣkeṇāniṣuṇā vrātyāḥ prasedhamānā yanti sa jyāhnoḍaḥ
8.6.d: धनुष्केणानिषुणा व्रात्याः प्रसेधमाना यन्ति स ज्याह्नोडः
8.6.m: The vrātyas go driving [enemies] off with a small bow without arrows; that is the 'jyāhnoḍa'.

8.6.s: vipathaśca phalakāstīrṇa iti prācyaratho nāstīrṇo vipathaḥ
8.6.d: विपथश्च फलकास्तीर्ण इति प्राच्यरथो नास्तीर्णो विपथः
8.6.m: Regarding the rule, "And a rough chariot covered with planks": a chariot of the easterners that is uncovered is a rough chariot.
It should be yoked with a trembling pair of a horse and a mule, according to Śāṇḍilya.
With any two horses or two mules whatsoever, according to Dhānañjayya.
Regarding the rule, "A black-bordered garment": it is black mixed with white threads, according to Śāṇḍilya.
It is white with a black fringe, according to Gautama.
I think it is simply black, according to Dhānañjayya.

8.6.s: yāvavikau dvābhyāmavibhyāmekaikaḥ krītaḥ syāttayoḥ pārśvashite kṛṣṇabalakṣe ajine syātām
8.6.d: यावविकौ द्वाभ्यामविभ्यामेकैकः क्रीतः स्यात्तयोः पार्श्वस्हिते कृष्णबलक्षे अजिने स्याताम्
8.6.m: Two sheepskins, each one bought with two sheep; in the flank-regions of the two there should be black and white skins.
'Balakṣa' is a word for white.
Regarding the rule, "That belongs to the householder": the householder should bring all this, and thirty-three [cows].
Two times thirty-three, according to Śāṇḍilya.
Regarding the rule, "Those of the others have valūka borders and string fringes": they should be garments of sheep's wool with red warp.
Regarding the expression 'having string fringes': they should have fringes of string; 'tūṣa' is a designation for a fringe.

8.6.s: dve dve dāmanī iti dve dve ekaikasya vasanasya daśe syātām
8.6.d: द्वे द्वे दामनी इति द्वे द्वे एकैकस्य वसनस्य दशे स्याताम्
8.6.m: Regarding the rule, "Two string fringes each": there should be two fringes for each single garment.

8.6.s: dve dve upānahāviti kṛṣṇāḥ karṇinya iti śāṇḍilyaḥ
8.6.d: द्वे द्वे उपानहाविति कृष्णाः कर्णिन्य इति शाण्डिल्यः
8.6.m: Regarding the rule, "Two sandals each": they are black and pointed, according to Śāṇḍilya.
Whatever kind they may be, according to Dhānañjayya.
The rule, "Two skins joined together," has been explained by the earlier two skins.

8.6.s: taccetareṣāmekaika āharettrayastrśitaṃ ca trayastrśitā gṛhapatimabhisamā yantīti hyāha
8.6.d: तच्चेतरेषामेकैक आहरेत्त्रयस्त्र्शितं च त्रयस्त्र्शिता गृहपतिमभिसमा यन्तीति ह्याह
8.6.m: And if each of the others should bring it, [each brings] thirty-three [cows], for [the Brāhmaṇa] says: 'Thirty-three [cows] come together to the householder.'
Those thirty-three should give [them] to the priests.

8.6.s: vrātyebhyo vrātyadhanāni ye vrātyacaryāyā aviratāḥ syurbrahmabandhave vā māgadhadeśīyāya yasmā etaddadati tasminneva mṛjānāyantīti hyāha
8.6.d: व्रात्येभ्यो व्रात्यधनानि ये व्रात्यचर्याया अविरताः स्युर्ब्रह्मबन्धवे वा मागधदेशीयाय यस्मा एतद्ददति तस्मिन्नेव मृजानायन्तीति ह्याह
8.6.m: [Or] the property of the Vrātyas to Vrātyas who have not ceased from the Vrātya life, or to an unworthy brāhmaṇa of the Magadha region; for it is said: 'Upon whomsoever they bestow this, upon him they wipe off [their guilt].'
Having sacrificed with the Vrātyastomas, they should take up the livelihood of the three Vedas.

8.6.s: taiṣāntata ūrddhvaṃ bhuñjītāpi cainān kāmaṃ yājayediti
8.6.d: तैषान्तत ऊर्द्ध्वं भुञ्जीतापि चैनान् कामं याजयेदिति
8.6.m: From then on, one may eat with them and also freely sacrifice for them.

8.7.m: In the Agniṣṭut [sacrifices], he should give of oxen, horses, [and] goats according to his ability, and likewise of gold.

8.7.s: kañcidarthamarhanyo na prāpnuyātsa trivṛtāṃ prathamena yajeta
8.7.d: कञ्चिदर्थमर्हन्यो न प्राप्नुयात्स त्रिवृतां प्रथमेन यजेत
8.7.m: One who, though deserving some object, does not attain it, should sacrifice with the first of the Trivṛt [rites].

8.7.s: tasya caturyugaśvaratho dakṣiṇā teṣāmekaḥ śyāvaḥ syāt
8.7.d: तस्य चतुर्युगश्वरथो दक्षिणा तेषामेकः श्यावः स्यात्
8.7.m: Its sacrificial fee is a chariot drawn by four horses; one of them should be dark-brown.

8.7.s: yaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ svarājānaḥ puraskurvīran sa vṛhaspatisavena yajeta
8.7.d: यं ब्राह्मणाः स्वराजानः पुरस्कुर्वीरन् स वृहस्पतिसवेन यजेत
8.7.m: He whom brāhmaṇas belonging to an independent territory place at their head should sacrifice with the Bṛhaspatisava.

8.7.s: tasya prātaḥsavane sanneṣu nārāś seṣvekādaśa dakṣiṇā vyādiśedṛtvigbhyo nāpākuryāt
8.7.d: तस्य प्रातःसवने सन्नेषु नाराश् सेष्वेकादश दक्षिणा व्यादिशेदृत्विग्भ्यो नापाकुर्यात्
8.7.m: At its morning pressing, when the nārāśaṃsa [cups] are set down, he should assign eleven sacrificial gifts to the priests; he should not drive [them] away.
Eleven at the third pressing; he should drive those away when the omentum of the anubandhyā [cow] has been offered.

8.7.s: tānyapyekādaśaikādaśaśatāni syuḥ sahasrāṇi vā nityastvaśvo madhyandine
8.7.d: तान्यप्येकादशैकादशशतानि स्युः सहस्राणि वा नित्यस्त्वश्वो मध्यन्दिने
8.7.m: Those also may be eleven times eleven hundreds or thousands, but a horse at the midday [pressing] is fixed.

8.7.s: ya enaṃ puraskurvīrannanvagbhūtavṛttiṃ tata ūrddhvaṃ teṣu varttayet
8.7.d: य एनं पुरस्कुर्वीरन्नन्वग्भूतवृत्तिं तत ऊर्द्ध्वं तेषु वर्त्तयेत्
8.7.m: From then on, he should conduct among those who place him at their head the livelihood of one who has attained obedience.
And they should address him as 'Sthapati.'
The Iṣu has been explained by the Śyena; but its consecration days and Upasad days belong to a one-day sacrifice.

8.8.s: sarvasvāreṇa yakṣyamāṇo dīkṣāprabhṛti prayateta yathā sautye'hani preyāmiti
8.8.d: सर्वस्वारेण यक्ष्यमाणो दीक्षाप्रभृति प्रयतेत यथा सौत्येऽहनि प्रेयामिति
8.8.m: One intending to sacrifice with the Sarvasvāra should strive, from the consecration onwards, thinking: 'May I pass away on the soma-pressing day.'
He should consume the portions everywhere by breath-consumption.
He should have them cast into water, or cause them to be poured out after the officiating priest.
Having mixed the soma with water, they should pour it out in the place of the mārjālīya [hearth].

8.8.s: ārbhave pavamāne stūyamāna udumbaryyā dakṣiṇā prāvṛto nipadyeta kṛṣṇājinamupastīryya dakṣiṇāśirāstadeva saṃgacchate tadeva mriyata iti
8.8.d: आर्भवे पवमाने स्तूयमान उदुम्बर्य्या दक्षिणा प्रावृतो निपद्येत कृष्णाजिनमुपस्तीर्य्य दक्षिणाशिरास्तदेव संगच्छते तदेव म्रियत इति
8.8.m: While the ārbhava pavamāna chant is being praised, having spread a black antelope skin south of the udumbara post, covered [all over], he should lie down with his head to the south; then he departs, then he dies.

8.8.s: etaṃ mṛtaṃ yajamānhavirbhiḥ saharjīṣeṇa yajñapātraiścāhavanīye prahṛtya pravrajeyuriti śāṇḍilyaḥ
8.8.d: एतं मृतं यजमान्हविर्भिः सहर्जीषेण यज्ञपात्रैश्चाहवनीये प्रहृत्य प्रव्रजेयुरिति शाण्डिल्यः
8.8.m: Having cast this dead patron of the sacrifice, along with the sacrificial offerings, the dregs, and the sacrificial vessels, into the āhavanīya fire, they should depart [wandering], says Śāṇḍilya.
They should complete the remainder, says Dhānañjayya.

8.8.s: samāpayeyuścediti śāṇḍilyāyano nediṣṭī tatkṛṣṇājinaṃ pratimucya yājamānaṃ kuryāt bhakṣāśca bhakṣayet
8.8.d: समापयेयुश्चेदिति शाण्डिल्यायनो नेदिष्टी तत्कृष्णाजिनं प्रतिमुच्य याजमानं कुर्यात् भक्षाश्च भक्षयेत्
8.8.m: If they complete [it], says Śāṇḍilyāyana, the next of kin, putting on that black antelope skin, should perform the duties of the patron of the sacrifice and consume the portions.

8.8.s: ṛtvijo yājamānaṃ kuryuḥ sarvahuto bhakṣān juhuyuriti dhānañjayyaḥ
8.8.d: ऋत्विजो याजमानं कुर्युः सर्वहुतो भक्षान् जुहुयुरिति धानञ्जय्यः
8.8.m: The priests should perform the duties of the patron of the sacrifice, [and] they should offer the portions as an entire oblation, says Dhānañjayya.
When the day is concluded, they should bring together the parts of the couch with the words: 'May they urge thee well.'
They should wash [them] with the words: 'May they rinse thee well.'
They should fashion [them] with the words: 'May they fashion thee well.'
They should weave [it] with the words: 'May they sharpen thee well.'

8.8.s: tanainamavabhṛthhṛtvā somopanahanena prachādyānūbandhyavapāyāhutāyāṃ dakṣiṇe vedyante keśaśmaśrūṇyasya vāpayeyuḥ
8.8.d: तनैनमवभृथ्हृत्वा सोमोपनहनेन प्रछाद्यानूबन्ध्यवपायाहुतायां दक्षिणे वेद्यन्ते केशश्मश्रूण्यस्य वापयेयुः
8.8.m: Having brought him to the concluding purificatory bath on it, covered with the soma-cloth, they should shave his hair and beard at the southern edge of the altar when the omentum of the anubandhyā cow has been offered.

8.8.s: anūbandhyaśeṣaṃ samāpya madhye devayajanasya citāṃ cinuyuḥ
8.8.d: अनूबन्ध्यशेषं समाप्य मध्ये देवयजनस्य चितां चिनुयुः
8.8.m: Having completed the remainder of the anubandhyā rite, they should build a pyre in the middle of the sacrificial ground.

8.8.s: paścādgārhapatyamupadadhyuḥ purastādāhavanīyaṃ paścimena gārhapatyaṃ dakṣiṇata āgnīdhrīyaṃ parihareyuḥ
8.8.d: पश्चाद्गार्हपत्यमुपदध्युः पुरस्तादाहवनीयं पश्चिमेन गार्हपत्यं दक्षिणत आग्नीध्रीयं परिहरेयुः
8.8.m: They should set down the gārhapatya [fire] to the west, the āhavanīya [fire] to the east; they should carry [it] around to the west of the gārhapatya fire, to the south of the āgnīdhra [hearth].
He should arrange with the sacrificial vessels [the body] placed on the pyre with its head to the south.
He should place the potsherds on the head;
and the cup with the gathered grains;
the vessel for holding the prāśitra portion on the forehead;

8.8.s: āsye hiraṇyamavadhāyānustaraṇikyā gaurmukhaṃ vapayā pracchādya tatrāgnihotrahavanīṃ tiraścīm
8.8.d: आस्ये हिरण्यमवधायानुस्तरणिक्या गौर्मुखं वपया प्रच्छाद्य तत्राग्निहोत्रहवनीं तिरश्चीम्
8.8.m: having placed gold in the mouth, [and] having covered the face with the omentum of the victim cow, [he should place] the agnihotra offering ladle there crosswise;
between the thighs the peg, the mill-stone and the lower grinding stone, and whatever else we shall not mention;
to the south of the right arm-pit, the mortar;

8.8.s: sarvāṇyuttānāni pṛṣadājyavanti kṛtvā sarvebhyo'gnibhya ulaparājīstṛṇuyuryathāsminnagnayaḥ samaveṣyantīti
8.8.d: सर्वाण्युत्तानानि पृषदाज्यवन्ति कृत्वा सर्वेभ्योऽग्निभ्य उलपराजीस्तृणुयुर्यथास्मिन्नग्नयः समवेष्यन्तीति
8.8.m: having made all [the vessels] turned upwards and filled with curd-butter, they should strew reed-straws from all the fires, so that the fires will unite in this [pyre].

8.8.s: āhavanīyāccetprathamameyāt brahmalokameṣyatīti vidyāt gārhapatyāddevalokaṃ dakṣiṇāgneḥ pitṛlokam
8.8.d: आहवनीयाच्चेत्प्रथममेयात् ब्रह्मलोकमेष्यतीति विद्यात् गार्हपत्याद्देवलोकं दक्षिणाग्नेः पितृलोकम्
8.8.m: If it reaches [him] first from the āhavanīya fire, one should know that he will go to the world of Brahman; if from the gārhapatya fire, to the world of the gods; if from the dakṣiṇāgni fire, to the world of the fathers.

8.8.s: kḷpteṣu yajñapātreṣu triśchandogaḥ parigāyet nāke suparṇamiti
8.8.d: कॢप्तेषु यज्ञपात्रेषु त्रिश्छन्दोगः परिगायेत् नाके सुपर्णमिति
8.8.m: When the sacrificial vessels have been arranged, the chanter of the Sāmaveda should sing around thrice: 'A golden-winged bird in the firmament...';
when it has blazed up, with either of the two: 'O Agni, be gracious...' [or] 'Great art thou...'.
This very procedure is for all who have set up the sacred fires.
If he survives, he should sacrifice with the Udavasānīyā rite.
From then on, he should seek to die by abstaining from food.
He should eat, he should indeed desire to live, says Dhānañjayya.
His sacrificial fee is cooked food.
He should begin the Cāturmāsya sacrifices on the full moon day of the month of Phālguna.
Another time is stated by the Brāhmaṇa.
On the day of sacrifice the Vaiśvadeva and Śunāsīrīya [offerings] should take place, and the Vāruṇapraghāsa should be the subsequent one.
The final one of the Sākamedhas takes place on the seasonal transition day.
The sacrificial gifts of the Śunāsīrīya are one hundred and twelve [cows].
Fifty for each single one of the other days.

8.9.m: In the Upahavya sacrifice, they should utter the names of the deities indirectly in their own places;
directly in places other than their own.
Everywhere they should omit the word 'deva' ('god').

8.9.s: hotā devo mahī mitrasyetyete hotā yajñe mahī yajñasyeti brūyurinduriti somam
8.9.d: होता देवो मही मित्रस्येत्येते होता यज्ञे मही यज्ञस्येति ब्रूयुरिन्दुरिति सोमम्
8.9.m: Instead of 'hotā devo' and 'mahī mitrasya', they should say 'hotā yajñe' and 'mahī yajñasya', [and] 'indu' instead of 'soma'.
The sacrificial gift is prescribed by the Brāhmaṇa.
And he should give something to the others.

8.9.s: ṛtapeye tasya dvādaśa dīkṣopasada iti tisra upasadaḥ
8.9.d: ऋतपेये तस्य द्वादश दीक्षोपसद इति तिस्र उपसदः
8.9.m: In the Ṛtapeya sacrifice, regarding the statement 'he has twelve consecration-upasad days', there are three upasads.
Regarding the statement 'he observes a ghee vow', he should consume [ghee] during the consecrations according to his capacity.

8.9.s: uttareṇottareṇa kāṇḍenopaitīti pṛthagupasatsvaṅguliparvabhiḥ pratilomaiḥ prāśnīyāditi dhānañjayyaḥ
8.9.d: उत्तरेणोत्तरेण काण्डेनोपैतीति पृथगुपसत्स्वङ्गुलिपर्वभिः प्रतिलोमैः प्राश्नीयादिति धानञ्जय्यः
8.9.m: Regarding the statement 'he approaches with each successive joint', he should consume [ghee] separately at each upasad with the finger joints in reverse order, so says Dhānañjayya.

8.9.s: ekāṅgulyā pṛthak parvabhiḥ sarvāndeśāścamasā mitāḥ syustairanulomairiti śaucivṛkṣiḥ
8.9.d: एकाङ्गुल्या पृथक् पर्वभिः सर्वान्देशाश्चमसा मिताः स्युस्तैरनुलोमैरिति शौचिवृक्षिः
8.9.m: With a single finger, using the joints separately, all cups measured according to the regions should be [drunk] with them in regular order, so says Śaucivṛkṣi.
In reverse order, so says Śāṇḍilya.

8.9.s: ṛtamuktvā prasarpantīti prasrapsyataḥ sado bhakṣayiṣyantaśca deva satyāni brūyuriyaṃ bhūmirasāvāditya iti
8.9.d: ऋतमुक्त्वा प्रसर्पन्तीति प्रस्रप्स्यतः सदो भक्षयिष्यन्तश्च देव सत्यानि ब्रूयुरियं भूमिरसावादित्य इति
8.9.m: Regarding the statement 'having spoken the cosmic order, they glide forward', those who are about to glide to the sadas and consume [soma] should utter divine truths: 'this is the earth', 'that is the sun'.
They should adapt the consumption formulas as having been drunk by whichever deities were worshipped with the cups, so says Śāṇḍilya.
For the Nārāśaṁsa [cups], however, [they recite the formulas] without modification.
Regarding the statement 'a cup of soma is the sacrificial gift', it should be of pressed [soma], for the cup is the measure with respect to that.

8.9.s: taṃ madhyandine savanamukhīyaiḥ sahonnayeyurjuhuyuścāsya huto deya iti hi brāhmaṇam
8.9.d: तं मध्यन्दिने सवनमुखीयैः सहोन्नयेयुर्जुहुयुश्चास्य हुतो देय इति हि ब्राह्मणम्
8.9.m: They should draw it up at midday along with the [cups] commencing the pressing and offer it, for the Brāhmaṇa says, 'Having been offered, it is to be given.'

8.9.s: taṃ dakṣiṇāvelāyāṃ pūrveṇāhavanīyamanirharanto vederdakṣiṇena sadohavirddhānāni hārayitvā pūrvayā dvārā sadaḥ praveśayeyuḥ
8.9.d: तं दक्षिणावेलायां पूर्वेणाहवनीयमनिर्हरन्तो वेदेर्दक्षिणेन सदोहविर्द्धानानि हारयित्वा पूर्वया द्वारा सदः प्रवेशयेयुः
8.9.m: At the time of the sacrificial gifts, without carrying it past the front of the āhavanīya, causing it to be borne south of the altar, the sadas, and the havirdhāna shed, they should bring it into the sadas through the eastern door.
When the day is concluded, he should give something to the officiating priests.

8.10.m: The sacrificial gift for the Dūṇāśa sacrifice is prescribed by the Brāhmaṇa.
Where it is stated, 'so many one hundred and twenty-eight weight-measures', he should give that many one hundred and twenty-eight [pieces] of twenty-four weight-measures each.
Regarding the statement 'a gold plate for the hotṛ', it is the ornament called a niṣka; he should give that.
Regarding the statement 'a garland for the udgātṛ', it should be made of gold.

8.10.s: vaiśyastome sadyo dugdhena payasā somaṃ miśraṅkuryuḥ prātaḥsavane śṛtena madhyandine dadhnā tṛtīyasavane
8.10.d: वैश्यस्तोमे सद्यो दुग्धेन पयसा सोमं मिश्रङ्कुर्युः प्रातःसवने शृतेन मध्यन्दिने दध्ना तृतीयसवने
8.10.m: In the Vaiśyastoma, they should mix the soma with fresh milk at the morning pressing, with boiled milk at the midday pressing, and with sour curds at the third pressing.

8.10.s: tasya dvādaśśataṃ dakṣiṇāḥ sahasraṃ vā yathārūpāḥ pañcaśāradīye paśava ālabhyante
8.10.d: तस्य द्वादश्शतं दक्षिणाः सहस्रं वा यथारूपाः पञ्चशारदीये पशव आलभ्यन्ते
8.10.m: Its sacrificial gifts are one hundred and twelve [cows] or a thousand, of the same appearance as the animals seized in the Pañcaśāradīya sacrifice.
Regarding the statement: 'He should sacrifice with the Tīvrasut for one who has over-purified soma':

8.10.s: ya iṣṭvā pāpīyān syāt sa somātipavita iti śāṇḍilyaḥ
8.10.d: य इष्ट्वा पापीयान् स्यात् स सोमातिपवित इति शाण्डिल्यः
8.10.m: he who, having sacrificed, becomes worse off is 'one who has over-purified soma', so says Śāṇḍilya.

8.10.s: yaḥ somaṃ pītvā chardayeta viricyeta veti dhānañjayyaḥ
8.10.d: यः सोमं पीत्वा छर्दयेत विरिच्येत वेति धानञ्जय्यः
8.10.m: He who, having drunk soma, vomits or is purged, so says Dhānañjayya.

8.10.s: tatra bhakṣāvṛtāścamasānavajighreyurachāvākastotreṇa stutvā bhakṣayeyurabhakṣayanta ṛtvijaścamasānavajighranti tānachāvākasya stotre bhakṣayantīti hyāha
8.10.d: तत्र भक्षावृताश्चमसानवजिघ्रेयुरछावाकस्तोत्रेण स्तुत्वा भक्षयेयुरभक्षयन्त ऋत्विजश्चमसानवजिघ्रन्ति तानछावाकस्य स्तोत्रे भक्षयन्तीति ह्याह
8.10.m: There, according to the procedure of consuming, they should smell the cups; having chanted with the achāvāka stotra, they should consume [them]; for [the Brāhmaṇa] says: 'Without consuming, the priests smell the cups; they consume them at the achāvāka's stotra.'
Regarding the statement 'they repeatedly pour soma into them', they should pour into those very cups that they smelled.

8.10.s: śatamāśiraṃ duhantīti dhenuśataṃ dohayitvā traidhaṃ vibhajya somaṃ miśraṃ kuryuryathā vaiśyastome
8.10.d: शतमाशिरं दुहन्तीति धेनुशतं दोहयित्वा त्रैधं विभज्य सोमं मिश्रं कुर्युर्यथा वैश्यस्तोमे
8.10.m: Regarding the statement 'they milk one hundred [cows] for the milk admixture', having caused one hundred milch cows to be milked, dividing [the milk] into three portions, they should mix the soma as in the Vaiśyastoma.

8.10.s: tasya tadeva dhenuśataṃ dakṣiṇāstā u eva dakṣiṇā iti hyāha
8.10.d: तस्य तदेव धेनुशतं दक्षिणास्ता उ एव दक्षिणा इति ह्याह
8.10.m: Its sacrificial gifts are that very hundred cows, for [the Brāhmaṇa] says: 'Those very ones are the sacrificial gifts.'

8.11.s: yaṃ brāhmaṇā rājānaśca puraskurvīran sa vājapeyena yajeta
8.11.d: यं ब्राह्मणा राजानश्च पुरस्कुर्वीरन् स वाजपेयेन यजेत
8.11.m: He whom brāhmaṇas and kings place at their head should sacrifice with the Vājapeya.

8.11.s: tasya paurṇamāsyāṃ dīkṣitvā trayodaśa dīkṣāḥ syuḥ
8.11.d: तस्य पौर्णमास्यां दीक्षित्वा त्रयोदश दीक्षाः स्युः
8.11.m: Having undergone consecration on the full moon day, he should have thirteen consecrations;
Having undergone consecration on the new moon day, for a month, so says Gautama.
For a year, with six upasads, and it should include the piling of the fire altar, so says Dhānañjayya.

8.11.s: pārṣṭikān stomān jyotiṣṭomatantre kalpayitvā tairjyotiṣṭomādibhistadvyavetaiḥ saṃvatsaraṃ pūrvapakṣeṣu yajeta trayodaśe pūrvapakṣe vājapeyeneṣṭvaitairevāvṛttairaparsaṃvatsaraṃ te yathotsāhadakṣiṇāḥ syuḥ
8.11.d: पार्ष्टिकान् स्तोमान् ज्योतिष्टोमतन्त्रे कल्पयित्वा तैर्ज्योतिष्टोमादिभिस्तद्व्यवेतैः संवत्सरं पूर्वपक्षेषु यजेत त्रयोदशे पूर्वपक्षे वाजपेयेनेष्ट्वैतैरेवावृत्तैरपर्संवत्सरं ते यथोत्साहदक्षिणाः स्युः
8.11.m: Having arranged the pṛṣṭha stomas according to the paradigm of the Jyotiṣṭoma, he should sacrifice during the bright fortnights for a year with those [rites] beginning with the Jyotiṣṭoma separated by it; having sacrificed with the Vājapeya in the thirteenth bright fortnight, [he should sacrifice] for the next year with these same [rites] repeated; their sacrificial gifts should be according to capacity.
He should sacrifice according to the procedure of the Rājasūya, so says Lāmakāyana.
The Trivṛt-Pañcadaśa should take the place of the Abhyārohaṇīya;
the Vājapeya, of the Abhiṣecanīya;
the Pañcadaśa-Trivṛt, of the Keśavapanīya;
two Jyotiṣṭomas [take the place] of the Vyuṣṭi and the Kṣatradhṛti.
He should sacrifice around it with the Bṛhaspatisava alone, both before and after, so says Dhānañjayya.
With the Jyotiṣṭoma one month before, and likewise after, so says Śāṇḍilyāyana.
He should sacrifice at the end with the Pratyavarohaṇīya alone, and not with any of the others, so says Gautama.
He should choose separate officiating priests, seventeen including the sadasya priest.
Its sacrificial gifts are female slaves, niṣkas, chariots, elephants, vehicles, cattle, and draught horses—seventeen of each kind;
or thousands, or hundreds of cattle;
or indeed seventeen cattle: they call this the Kuru-Vājapeya.
He should divide them equally among the officiating priests.
Or [give] the best share to the central officiants.

8.11.s: yena rathenājindhāvettamudgātre dadyādāsandīñca sāstaraṇāṃ yāmabhiṣikta ārohet
8.11.d: येन रथेनाजिन्धावेत्तमुद्गात्रे दद्यादासन्दीञ्च सास्तरणां यामभिषिक्त आरोहेत्
8.11.m: The chariot on which he ran the race he should give to the udgātṛ priest, and also the wicker chair with its cushion on which he sat when consecrated.
The goat skin with the golden ornament on which he sat when consecrated, [he should give] to the hotṛ priest.
The bridle made of cloth, to the adhvaryu priest.
A golden bowl filled with honey, to the brahman priest.
Or golden husks mixed with honey in a bowl of bronze.

8.12.m: His observances: he should follow the conduct of the warrior class.
Dismounting, greeting, walking behind, and sharing a bed—these he should avoid with those who have not performed the Vājapeya sacrifice.
With those who have performed the Vājapeya sacrifice, according to age.
Having performed the Pratyavarohaṇīya rite, he should not observe these vows: so says Lāmakāyana.

8.12.s: prākṛtaeva vājapeya ekiprabhṛtīdvyuttarān saptadaśatrayastriṃśāntān stomān kalpayetsamayūro nīkarṣītyācakṣate
8.12.d: प्राकृतएव वाजपेय एकिप्रभृतीद्व्युत्तरान् सप्तदशत्रयस्त्रिंशान्तान् स्तोमान् कल्पयेत्समयूरो नीकर्षीत्याचक्षते
8.12.m: In the primary Vājapeya itself, one should arrange the stomans beginning with one and increasing by two, ending with seventeen and thirty-three: they call this Samayūra Nīkarṣin.
Its bahiṣpavamāna chant is on 'Sing unto him' (upāsmai gāyata).
The chant of the brahman priest is the same; having sacrificed with this rite, one ascends to the heavenly world: so says Dhānañjayya.
A Jyotiṣṭoma atirātra sacrifice without the ṣoḍaśin, or a non-atirātra sacrifice with the ṣoḍaśin.
Its Bṛhat should be a seventeen-fold stotra on fifteen-fold strophic verses.
Its brahman's chant is the Ābhīvarta on an anuṣṭubh verse; one should adapt the Yajñāyajñīya melody, with the Bṛhat as the agniṣṭoma-sāman.
The chant of the brahman priest is a twenty-five-fold form of the pṛṣṭha lauds, or the chant of the acchāvāka priest is twenty-four-fold, and the other is the reverse.

8.12.s: etasya vaiva catustrśiāni pṛṣṭhānyagniṣṭomasāma ca saptadaśamitarat
8.12.d: एतस्य वैव चतुस्त्र्शिआनि पृष्ठान्यग्निष्टोमसाम च सप्तदशमितरत्

8.12.s: naiteṣāṃ kaścana vājapeya iti gautamo yajamānaścaibhirna vājapeyadakṣiṇā dadyāditi dadyāditi
8.12.d: नैतेषां कश्चन वाजपेय इति गौतमो यजमानश्चैभिर्न वाजपेयदक्षिणा दद्यादिति दद्यादिति
8.12.m: None of these is a Vājapeya: so says Gautama; and through these, the patron of the sacrifice should not give the sacrificial gifts of the Vājapeya, he should not give.

9.1.m: A king should sacrifice with the Rājasūya.
He should undergo consecration on the first [day] of the Phālgunī half-month for the Abhyārohaṇīya Jyotiṣṭoma.
Its consecration is one [day]; the sacrificial gifts are one hundred and twelve [cows].
After a year, he should sacrifice with the Abhiṣecanīya at that very same time.
If so, two for the Abhyārohaṇīya as well.
One for the Abhyārohaṇīya and three for the Abhiṣecanīya: so says Śāṇḍilya; but he should undergo consecration on the thirteenth day of the dark half-month.

9.1.s: tasya dakṣiṇā dvātrśitaṃ madhyataḥ kāribhyaḥ sahasrāṇi dadyādekaikasmai
9.1.d: तस्य दक्षिणा द्वात्र्शितं मध्यतः कारिभ्यः सहस्राणि दद्यादेकैकस्मै
9.1.m: Its sacrificial gifts: he should give thirty-two thousand [cows] to the central officiants, to each one.
Sixteen [thousand] to the prastotṛ, maitrāvaruṇa, pratiprasthātṛ, and brāhmaṇācchaṃsin priests.
Eight [thousand] to the pratihartṛ, potṛ, neṣṭṛ, and acchāvāka priests; these are the third-share recipients.
They should bring in his powerless relatives along with their possessions.
He should overpower them at the time of the sacrificial gifts.
They themselves should bring them back, saying, 'Be victorious, O King!'
He should give a third of their wealth to the officiating priests.
At the Daśapeya, a third to those who have glided forward in order.
The remainder he should surrender back to them.
They should become warriors ineligible for royal consecration from that point onward.

9.1.s: teneṣṭvā na sākṣādavabhṛthamabhyaveyāt kṛṣṇaviṣāṇaṃ kṛṣṇājinapādaṃ vāvadadhyāt
9.1.d: तेनेष्ट्वा न साक्षादवभृथमभ्यवेयात् कृष्णविषाणं कृष्णाजिनपादं वावदध्यात्
9.1.m: Having sacrificed with it, he should not go directly down to the concluding purificatory bath; he should put down a black horn or the foot of a black antelope skin.

9.2.s: taddīkṣita eva daśāhe tato daśapeyena yajeta
9.2.d: तद्दीक्षित एव दशाहे ततो दशपेयेन यजेत
9.2.m: Remaining under that same consecration, on the tenth day from then, he should sacrifice with the Daśapeya.
Its Brāhmaṇa passage says: 'Ten by ten, they approach the cup.'
With the subrahmaṇya priest as the fourth, they should consume the udgātṛ priest's cup, six other [priests sharing it].
In the same manner, [others share] each of the other cups until ten are complete, excluding the patron of the sacrifice's cup.
They should glide forward after recounting ten maternal ancestors and ten paternal ancestors, for it says: 'Down to the tenth generation of men.'
Where they encounter a non-brāhmaṇa woman, they should complete the ten by repeating a brāhmaṇa woman [in the line].
And if they do not remember, [they should begin] from where they remember.
Together with the officiating priests, they should wait upon the dhiṣṇya hearths.
With 'A garland for the udgātṛ,' [the patron of the sacrifice] should fasten around him, who is about to glide for the bahiṣpavamāna chant, a golden garland with three lotus blossoms.

9.2.s: āstāva upaviṣṭāya yajamāna audakīṃ dvādaśapuṣkarāṃ yāsya vā syāt
9.2.d: आस्ताव उपविष्टाय यजमान औदकीं द्वादशपुष्करां यास्य वा स्यात्
9.2.m: When he is seated at the chanting place, the patron of the sacrifice [gives] one of water-lilies with twelve lotus blossoms, or whichever one he has.
Having chanted with the bahiṣpavamāna chant, he should surrender the water jar to the patron of the sacrifice alone.

9.2.s: itarayā pratimuktayā sarvamahaḥ kṛtvā tāsa eva haret
9.2.d: इतरया प्रतिमुक्तया सर्वमहः कृत्वा तास एव हरेत्
9.2.m: Having spent the entire day with the other [garland] put on, he should take just those [two garlands away].
Regarding '[two] mirrors for the two adhvaryu priests': a golden one should be for the adhvaryu on the south, a silver one for the pratiprasthātṛ on the north.
Regarding 'a garment for the potṛ': it should be of cotton.
Regarding 'a barāsī-cloth for the neṣṭṛ': it should be of linen.
The others are known through the Brāhmaṇa itself.
Having emerged from its concluding purificatory bath, he should observe the divine vows for a year.
He should rub [his body] without submerging [in water].
He may have his beard shaved, but not the hair of his head.
He should lie down in the fire-house on a tiger-skin with the fur turned up.
Day after day, he should place kindling sticks [on the fire].
Non-brāhmaṇas in his realm should not shave.
And they should not cut the hair of horses.

9.2.s: brāhmaṇāstu yathābhipretaṃ ye ca tānanu syuḥ
9.2.d: ब्राह्मणास्तु यथाभिप्रेतं ये च ताननु स्युः
9.2.m: Brāhmaṇas, however, [may act] according to their wish, as well as those who are under them.

9.3.s: saṃvatsarādūrddhvaṃ keśavapanīyāya dīkṣeta yasmin kāle'bhiṣecanīyena yajeta
9.3.d: संवत्सरादूर्द्ध्वं केशवपनीयाय दीक्षेत यस्मिन् कालेऽभिषेचनीयेन यजेत
9.3.m: After the year, he should receive consecration for the Keśavapanīya at the time when he sacrificed with the Abhiṣecanīya.
Its atirātra sacrifice is on the full moon.

9.3.s: daśapeyeneṣṭvā ya uttaraḥ pūrvapakṣastasminneva keśavapanīyena yajeteti dhānañjayyaḥ paurṇṇamāsyāñcaivātirātraḥ
9.3.d: दशपेयेनेष्ट्वा य उत्तरः पूर्वपक्षस्तस्मिन्नेव केशवपनीयेन यजेतेति धानञ्जय्यः पौर्ण्णमास्याञ्चैवातिरात्रः
9.3.m: Having sacrificed with the Daśapeya, he should sacrifice with the Keśavapanīya in the very next bright fortnight, and the atirātra sacrifice is also on the full moon—so says Dhānañjayya.
Its sacrificial gifts are a thousand [cows].

9.3.s: tasyodavasānīyayeṣṭvāniṣṭvā paurṇṇamāsena vyuṣṭidvirātrāya dīkṣetāmāvāsyāyāṃ pūrvamahariti ceccikīrṣet
9.3.d: तस्योदवसानीययेष्ट्वानिष्ट्वा पौर्ण्णमासेन व्युष्टिद्विरात्राय दीक्षेतामावास्यायां पूर्वमहरिति चेच्चिकीर्षेत्
9.3.m: Having sacrificed with its Udavasānīyā offering, without having sacrificed with the full-moon offering, he should receive consecration for the Vyuṣṭidvirātra, if he intends to make the first day fall on the new moon.
If [he intends to make it fall] on the full moon, he should receive consecration in that very bright fortnight.
In both options, the second day falls on the sacrificial day.
Regarding 'the second day on the Vyaṣṭakā': they designate the first three [days] of the dark fortnight as Vyaṣṭakās.

9.3.s: ubhe vā pūrvapakṣe syātāṃ ye eva samānapakṣe puṇyāhanī syātāṃ tayoreva kāryyamiti hyāyeti
9.3.d: उभे वा पूर्वपक्षे स्यातां ये एव समानपक्षे पुण्याहनी स्यातां तयोरेव कार्य्यमिति ह्यायेति
9.3.m: Or both may be in the bright fortnight; for it is stated: 'One should perform it on whichever two auspicious days are in the same fortnight.'
The sacrificial gifts are explained by the previous [rite].

9.3.s: tasminneva pūrvapakṣe kṣatrasya dhṛtinā yajetāvakāśaścet syāt
9.3.d: तस्मिन्नेव पूर्वपक्षे क्षत्रस्य धृतिना यजेतावकाशश्चेत् स्यात्
9.3.m: In that same bright fortnight he should sacrifice with the Kṣatrasyadhṛti, if there is an opportunity.
If not available, in whichever bright fortnight is the next one.
It is explained by the Abhyārohaṇīya.

9.3.s: tayoḥ pṛthaksahasre dakṣiṇā iti gautamadhānañjayyau dve ca sahasre keśavapanīye tathā vyuṣṭau
9.3.d: तयोः पृथक्सहस्रे दक्षिणा इति गौतमधानञ्जय्यौ द्वे च सहस्रे केशवपनीये तथा व्युष्टौ
9.3.m: The sacrificial gifts for those two are a thousand [cows] each—so say Gautama and Dhānañjayya; and two thousand in the Keśavapanīya, likewise in the Vyuṣṭi.
Four [thousand] in the Abhiṣecanīya, says Gautama.

9.3.s: pañca dhānañjayyo nityaṃ tvabalānāṃ jñātīnāṃ vittama
9.3.d: पञ्च धानञ्जय्यो नित्यं त्वबलानां ज्ञातीनां वित्तम
9.3.m: Five [thousand], says Dhānañjayya; but constantly [he should seize] the property of weak relatives.

9.4.m: In the Rājya rite, he should give groups of twenty-one according to his capacity, but he should sacrifice all around before and after with an animal victim to Indra—a bull.

9.4.s: virāji daśavargānyathotsāhaṃ dadyādāgneyena tu paśunā purastādupariṣṭācca pariyajeta
9.4.d: विराजि दशवर्गान्यथोत्साहं दद्यादाग्नेयेन तु पशुना पुरस्तादुपरिष्टाच्च परियजेत
9.4.m: In the Virāj rite, he should give groups of ten according to his capacity, but he should sacrifice all around before and after with an animal victim to Agni.
Its sacrificial gifts are one hundred and twenty-four.

9.4.s: pūrve vayasyuccāvacānyājayitvopanīya vā tebhyaḥ samāvartsyan punaḥstomena yajeta
9.4.d: पूर्वे वयस्युच्चावचान्याजयित्वोपनीय वा तेभ्यः समावर्त्स्यन् पुनःस्तोमेन यजेत
9.4.m: Having officiated for high and low, or having initiated them, in his earlier life, when he is about to return home from them, he should sacrifice with the Punaḥstoma.
Its sacrificial gifts are twelve pairs—so says Dhānañjayya.

9.4.s: punaḥ sskṛto rathaḥ punarutsyūtśāmūlaṃ punardhenuḥ punarvatsa iti śāṇḍilya eteṣāṃ yathotsāhaṃ dadyāt
9.4.d: पुनः स्स्कृतो रथः पुनरुत्स्यूत्शामूलं पुनर्धेनुः पुनर्वत्स इति शाण्डिल्य एतेषां यथोत्साहं दद्यात्
9.4.m: A repaired chariot, a resewn woollen garment, a cow that has calved again, a renewed calf—so says Śāṇḍilya; of these he should give according to his capacity.
In the two Catuṣṭomas, he should give one-hoofed animals according to his capacity in the former, and both kinds [one-hoofed and cloven-hoofed] in the latter.
Both of them should conclude in seven days, and [take place] in spring.

9.4.s: arddhamāsa enāvantareṇa syānmāso vā saṃvatsaro vā
9.4.d: अर्द्धमास एनावन्तरेण स्यान्मासो वा संवत्सरो वा
9.4.m: Between them there should be half a month, or a month, or a year.
For each of the two he should give groups of twenty-four according to his capacity.
In the two Apaciti rites, [the gifts are] separately two horse-drawn chariots yoked with four [horses],
accompanied on both sides by bronze armour.
The horses should be worth a hundred, or bought for a hundred.
A king should sacrifice with these two—so says Dhānañjayya.
Anyone who is desirous of respect—so says Śāṇḍilya.
By means of the one-day vow, the approach for the two stomas of Agni is stated.

9.4.s: tayoḥ pṛthakcatvāri dhānyācitāni dakṣiṇāḥ ṣaḍgavāni pūrvasya caturgavānyuttarasya
9.4.d: तयोः पृथक्चत्वारि धान्याचितानि दक्षिणाः षड्गवानि पूर्वस्य चतुर्गवान्युत्तरस्य
9.4.m: The sacrificial gifts for those two are separately four cart-loads of grain; [drawn by] six oxen for the former, and [drawn by] four oxen for the latter.
In the Ṛṣabha sacrifice, the sacrificial gifts are one hundred and twelve bulls, [or] a thousand.

9.4.s: avidyamāneṣu katipayā apyṛṣabhāḥ syuḥ sāṇḍā itare vatsatarāḥ
9.4.d: अविद्यमानेषु कतिपया अप्यृषभाः स्युः साण्डा इतरे वत्सतराः
9.4.m: When they are not available, there may be even a few bulls, while the others are uncastrated young bullocks.

9.4.s: vaiśyaṃ yaṃ viśaḥ svarājānaḥ puraskurvīran sa gosavena yajeta
9.4.d: वैश्यं यं विशः स्वराजानः पुरस्कुर्वीरन् स गोसवेन यजेत
9.4.m: A vaiśya whom the self-ruling commoners set at their head should sacrifice with the Gosava.
It is explained by the Bṛhaspatisava.
Its sacrificial gifts, however, are ten thousand [cows].

9.4.s: sakhāyo bhrātaro vā ye sampādayeyuste marutstomena yajeran
9.4.d: सखायो भ्रातरो वा ये सम्पादयेयुस्ते मरुत्स्तोमेन यजेरन्
9.4.m: Friends or brothers who wish to prosper together should sacrifice with the Marutstoma.

9.4.s: tasya dakṣiṇā yathārūpāḥ pañcaśāradīye paśava ālabhyante teṣāṃ yathotsāhaṃ dadyuḥ
9.4.d: तस्य दक्षिणा यथारूपाः पञ्चशारदीये पशव आलभ्यन्ते तेषां यथोत्साहं दद्युः
9.4.m: Its sacrificial gifts [should be cattle] of the same form as the animals slaughtered in the Pañcaśāradīya sacrifice; they should give them according to their capacity.
Dhānañjayya says: of whatever kind they may be.
The Kulāya of Indra and Agni has the property of [the patron's] family as its sacrificial gift.
A king and his domestic chaplain should sacrifice together with the stoma of Indra and Agni.

9.4.s: gāyatrīsampannā dakṣiṇā brāhmaṇo dadyāt jagatīsampannā rājā
9.4.d: गायत्रीसम्पन्ना दक्षिणा ब्राह्मणो दद्यात् जगतीसम्पन्ना राजा
9.4.m: The brāhmaṇa should give sacrificial gifts measured by the gāyatrī [number, twenty-four], and the king measured by the jagatī [number, forty-eight].
If, however, they sacrifice separately according to their wish, their sacrificial gifts are just the same.
One who desires cattle, or one who is performing a malevolent rite, should sacrifice with the two Vighanas.
As to whether [the chanting] has the Somasāman or the Ātharvaṇa, he should use the Ātharvaṇa in the sacrifice of one desiring cattle, and the Somasāman in that of one performing a malevolent rite.
The sacrificial gifts of one desiring cattle are measured by the bṛhatī [number, thirty-six].
The two [rites] for one performing a malevolent rite are explained by the Iṣu rite.
He should perform a malevolent rite against a king with the Saṃdaṃśa, and against a whole territory with the Vajra.
If he performs a malevolent rite against a king, he may employ these two alternatively.
At the conclusion, he should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma itself, for the sake of appeasement, for the sake of appeasement.

9.5.m: The multi-day sacrifices have their consecration on a full-moon day and conclude with the end of a month.
When there is an accumulation of soma-pressing days, there is a reduction of the consecration [days].

9.5.s: sarve'tirātrā ahīnā dvirātraprabhṛtayaścāhargaṇā aśvamedhādanye sahasradakṣiṇāḥ prāk catūrātrebhyaḥ
9.5.d: सर्वेऽतिरात्रा अहीना द्विरात्रप्रभृतयश्चाहर्गणा अश्वमेधादन्ये सहस्रदक्षिणाः प्राक् चतूरात्रेभ्यः
9.5.m: All atirātra multi-day sacrifices and day-sequences beginning with the two-day rite, other than the Aśvamedha, have one thousand [cows] as sacrificial gifts, prior to the four-day rites.
For those beginning with that [four-day rite], there are more, according to the accumulation of soma-pressing days.
He should give them equally divided among all the days.
If equal division is impossible, the largest portion [should be given] on the last day.
In the eleven-day sacrifice, he should give ten thousand [cows].
Nine hundred on each of the preceding days, and one thousand on the last day.
In the Aptoryāma, the embryonic insertions are made according to the ritual procedure.
Or the Rathantara is the [first] pṛṣṭha laud.
In its place is the Vājajit, based on the bṛhatī.
The Bṛhat and the Vāravantīya are the subsequent two pṛṣṭha lauds.
The Vāravantīya is on the verses of the Kāleya.
These very ones are the embryonic insertions in the pṛṣṭha lauds.
Dhānañjayya says: he should make the embryonic insertions in the ājyastotras using the Vaiśvajita melodies, and in the ukthastotras using the Ṣāṣṭhika melodies.
Śaucivṛkṣi says: just as it has been made according to the Ārṣeyakalpa.
Śāṇḍilya says: in the Jyotiṣṭoma or in the Atirātra, he should introduce the additional stotras, having the Ṣoḍaśin.

9.5.s: ta eva garbhāḥ pṛṣṭheṣu yajñāyajñīyañca bṛhadgarbham
9.5.d: त एव गर्भाः पृष्ठेषु यज्ञायज्ञीयञ्च बृहद्गर्भम्
9.5.m: These very ones are the embryonic insertions in the pṛṣṭha lauds, and the Yajñāyajñīya containing the Bṛhat as an embryo.

9.6.s: atha ṣaṣṭhī prakāśa tirātrāṇāṃ prathame'hani vaṣaṭkāribhyo dadyāt grāvastute ca
9.6.d: अथ षष्ठी प्रकाश तिरात्राणां प्रथमेऽहनि वषट्कारिभ्यो दद्यात् ग्रावस्तुते च
9.6.m: Now the sixth [section]. In the three-day rites of the light type, he should give [gifts] on the first day to the vaṣaṭ-makers and to the grāvastut priest.
He should give one hundred [cows] to each of the chief priests;
fifty to those entitled to half-shares;
among those entitled to third-shares, twenty to the potṛ priest, and likewise to the neṣṭr priest;
thirty to the other two, and to the āgnīdhra priest among those entitled to fourth-shares;
nine to the unnetṛ priest, and ten to the other two.
Day after day, however, he should give equally to the unnetṛ priest.

9.6.s: daśa sadasyāya prathame'hani saptatiṃ dvitīye vśitiṃ tṛtīye
9.6.d: दश सदस्याय प्रथमेऽहनि सप्ततिं द्वितीये व्शितिं तृतीये
9.6.m: Ten to the sadasya priest on the first day, seventy on the second, and twenty on the third.
Ten each to those who proclaim their lineage, who are mentioned in the Brāhmaṇa.
Two learned priests on the two preceding days, and an unlearned one on the last day.

9.6.s: daśaśat śiṣyante tā ṛtvigbhyo dadyāt prasarpakebhyo vā
9.6.d: दशशत् शिष्यन्ते ता ऋत्विग्भ्यो दद्यात् प्रसर्पकेभ्यो वा
9.6.m: Ten and a hundred [i.e., one hundred and ten] remain: he should give them to the priests or to the wandering spectators.
The thousandth cow, on the middle day, [belongs] to the brahman priest and to the āgnīdhra priest.
White, black, and red are her appearances.
He should allot [it saying]: 'Ten parts to the brahman priest, five to the āgnīdhra priest, and one is mine.'

9.6.s: tāmanyayā gavā niṣkrīya dakṣiṇe'syāḥ karṇe gonāmāni japitvā goṣvapi sṛjeta
9.6.d: तामन्यया गवा निष्क्रीय दक्षिणेऽस्याः कर्णे गोनामानि जपित्वा गोष्वपि सृजेत
9.6.m: Having redeemed her with another cow, and having whispered the names of cows into her right ear, he should release her among the cows.
The rule for the Jyotiṣṭoma should apply to that which is part of the Dvādaśāha, on account of its being handed down immediately after.
And because of the appearance of its characteristic marks, just as in the case of the pṛṣṭha lauds.
And because of its repeated transmission at the beginning of ahīna and ekāha sacrifices.
Not so: for those enjoined under different contexts, there can be no connection merely on account of contiguity, as in the case of the Upahavya and the Ṛtapeya.
And the employment of a characteristic mark is for the sake of something else, as in the case of the Śakvarī verses on the sixth day.
The repeated transmission is for the sake of laying down the remainder.

9.7.m: In that independent [sacrifice], there should be an ahīna night, for it is enjoined without distinction in the ahīna sacrifices.
However, it must be the archetypal [night], because it is taught within its own heading.
The prescription without distinction applies to the remainder, as in the case of the fourfold portioning.
By this is stated the replacement of the syllable om with [the word] 'vāk' in the Rathantara.
There should rather be combination, because their purposes are distinct: for the word 'vāk' is for appeasing the prastāva, while the syllable om belongs to the beginning of the udgītha.
However, 'vāk' comes first; thus the proximity is according to its purpose.
Or it is subsequent, because of its rule being placed later and on account of customary practice.

9.7.s: ekastomeṣu vaidatrirātre ca svastomā rātriḥ syāttathā sandhirubhay hyavikāreṇa varttate
9.7.d: एकस्तोमेषु वैदत्रिरात्रे च स्वस्तोमा रात्रिः स्यात्तथा सन्धिरुभय् ह्यविकारेण वर्त्तते
9.7.m: In [rites] of a single stoma and in the Vaida-trirātra, the night should have its own stoma, and likewise the sandhi chant; for both proceed without modification.

9.7.s: parāktvañca trivṛto'nyatra sandhernopapadyate trivṛtātirātreṇeti ca viśeṣacodanā
9.7.d: पराक्त्वञ्च त्रिवृतोऽन्यत्र सन्धेर्नोपपद्यते त्रिवृतातिरात्रेणेति च विशेषचोदना
9.7.m: And continuing through [in the series] of the Trivṛt is not appropriate anywhere other than at the sandhi chant, and there is the specific injunction: 'with the Trivṛt-atirātra'.

9.7.s: vṛttyapekṣā cādeśena vidyate yathā ṣoḍaśaṃ prathamaṃ rātriṣāmeti
9.7.d: वृत्त्यपेक्षा चादेशेन विद्यते यथा षोडशं प्रथमं रात्रिषामेति
9.7.m: And an expectation of modification is found through specific designation, as in: 'the sixteenth [laud] is the first of the night lauds'.
According to the purpose-statement, there is insertion in the sandhi chant.

9.7.s: brāhmaṇamājyadohānāmagnimupanidhāyaṃ stuvata iti hoturdhiṣṇye'gniṃ dhārayeyuḥ prathame'hani yaṃ madhyandina ānayeyuḥ
9.7.d: ब्राह्मणमाज्यदोहानामग्निमुपनिधायं स्तुवत इति होतुर्धिष्ण्येऽग्निं धारयेयुः प्रथमेऽहनि यं मध्यन्दिन आनयेयुः
9.7.m: There is the Brāhmaṇa passage: 'Having placed the fire near the Ājyadohas, they chant'; they should maintain the fire at the Hotṛ's hearth on the first day, which they bring at midday;
At the morning pressing on the subsequent two days.
At the time of the stotra, they should make it blaze up.

9.7.s: tamanumantrayetāgnirasi vaiśvānaro namaste'stu mā mā hīsīriti
9.7.d: तमनुमन्त्रयेताग्निरसि वैश्वानरो नमस्तेऽस्तु मा मा हीसीरिति
9.7.m: He should accompany it with the formula: 'You are Agni Vaiśvānara; homage be to you; do not injure me.'

9.8.m: One who desires the thriving of a thousand [cattle] should perform the Śabalī offering.

9.8.s: nātrirātrayājīti śāṇḍilyastrirātro vā etāṃ pradāpayatīti hyāha
9.8.d: नात्रिरात्रयाजीति शाण्डिल्यस्त्रिरात्रो वा एतां प्रदापयतीति ह्याह
9.8.m: 'Not one who has not performed a Trirātra,' says Śāṇḍilya, for [the scripture] says: 'The Trirātra indeed causes this to be given.'
'Whoever desires the thriving of a thousand,' says Dhānañjayya.

9.8.s: vasante prathamāyāṃ pūrvapakṣasya keśaśmaśrūṇi vāpayitvāhataṃ vasanaṃ paridhāyānantarhite sthaṇḍile dvādaśa rātrīradhaḥ śayīta taptaṃ kṣīraṃ pivan
9.8.d: वसन्ते प्रथमायां पूर्वपक्षस्य केशश्मश्रूणि वापयित्वाहतं वसनं परिधायानन्तर्हिते स्थण्डिले द्वादश रात्रीरधः शयीत तप्तं क्षीरं पिवन्
9.8.m: In the spring, on the first day of the bright fortnight, having shaved his head and beard and put on an unwashed garment, he should sleep on the bare ground without covering for twelve nights, drinking hot milk.
His fire should be kept continuously burning in his dwelling.
No one else other than a friend who executes his commands should enter after him.

9.8.s: dvādaśyā upavyuṣaṃ parisamuhyāgniṃ paristīryyaudumbara idhmaḥ syātsruksruvau ca tathā camasastasmāddadhimadhusarpiriti sruveṇa sruci gṛhṇīyāccaturgṛhītamaṣṭagṛhītaṃ vā
9.8.d: द्वादश्या उपव्युषं परिसमुह्याग्निं परिस्तीर्य्यौदुम्बर इध्मः स्यात्स्रुक्स्रुवौ च तथा चमसस्तस्माद्दधिमधुसर्पिरिति स्रुवेण स्रुचि गृह्णीयाच्चतुर्गृहीतमष्टगृहीतं वा
9.8.m: At dawn on the twelfth [day], having swept around the fire and spread the grass about, the firewood should be of udumbara wood, as should the offering-ladle and spoon, and likewise the cup; from that, he should take curd, honey, and clarified butter into the sruc with the sruva, taking four or eight ladlefSphuls.
He should offer it with: 'You are Śabalī, the ocean.'

9.8.s: sruci yaḥ śeṣaḥ syāttaṃ camasa ānīya prāśnīyāt
9.8.d: स्रुचि यः शेषः स्यात्तं चमस आनीय प्राश्नीयात्
9.8.m: Whatever remainder is left in the ladle, having poured it into the cup, he should consume it.
Having washed the sruc, the sruva, and the cup, he should deposit them.
'He should throw them into the fire right there,' says Śāṇḍilyāyana.

9.8.s: prāṅ vodaṅvā grāmānniṣkramya yatra grāmyasya paśornāśṛṇuyāttadaraṇyaṃ paretya darbhastambamālabhya śabali śabalīti triḥ paramakaṇṭhena krośet
9.8.d: प्राङ् वोदङ्वा ग्रामान्निष्क्रम्य यत्र ग्राम्यस्य पशोर्नाशृणुयात्तदरण्यं परेत्य दर्भस्तम्बमालभ्य शबलि शबलीति त्रिः परमकण्ठेन क्रोशेत्
9.8.m: Going out from the village towards the east or the north, having reached that forest where he cannot hear any domestic animal, touching a clump of darbha grass, he should shout at the top of his voice three times: 'Śabalī, Śabalī!'

9.8.s: yadanyacchuno gardabhādvā prativāśyeta samṛddhaṃ karmeti vidyāt
9.8.d: यदन्यच्छुनो गर्दभाद्वा प्रतिवाश्येत समृद्धं कर्मेति विद्यात्
9.8.m: If any animal other than a dog or a donkey answers with a call, he should know: 'The rite is successful.'
Thus he should repeat it up to the third year if there is no response.

9.8.s: prathamataścettu śvā gardabho vā prativāśyeta na paśūnāmāśāstīti vidyāt
9.8.d: प्रथमतश्चेत्तु श्वा गर्दभो वा प्रतिवाश्येत न पशूनामाशास्तीति विद्यात्
9.8.m: If, however, at first a dog or a donkey answers with a call, he should know: 'There is no hope for cattle.'
And [likewise] if there is no response up to the third [year].
The appeasement is the Vāmadevya melody; the appeasement is the Vāmadevya melody.

9.9.m: A king should sacrifice with the Aśvamedha.
Its procedure is Gautama's view as in the Mahāvrata.
Its upasad days, however, belong to the ahīna type.

9.9.s: dīkṣitvāśvamutsṛjet śvetaṃ kṛṣṇamaṇḍalamahṇo rūpaṃ yojavena sampannaḥ
9.9.d: दीक्षित्वाश्वमुत्सृजेत् श्वेतं कृष्णमण्डलमह्णो रूपं योजवेन सम्पन्नः
9.9.m: Having consecrated himself, he should release the horse, which is white with black spots, the form of the day, endowed with speed.

9.9.s: tamanāvarttayanto digbhyaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ rakṣitvā rājakraye badhnīyuḥ
9.9.d: तमनावर्त्तयन्तो दिग्भ्यः संवत्सरं रक्षित्वा राजक्रये बध्नीयुः
9.9.m: Guarding it for a year from the quarters without turning it back, they should tie it at the king-buying [rite].
'The commencement is in summer,' says Dhānañjayya.

9.9.s: caitravaiśākhayoranyatarasya saptamyāmaṣṭamyāṃ vā madhyataḥkāriṇa ṛtvijo brahmaudanaṃ bhojayitvā tebhyaḥ pṛthaksahasrāṇi dadyāt
9.9.d: चैत्रवैशाखयोरन्यतरस्य सप्तम्यामष्टम्यां वा मध्यतःकारिण ऋत्विजो ब्रह्मौदनं भोजयित्वा तेभ्यः पृथक्सहस्राणि दद्यात्
9.9.m: On either the seventh or eighth day of Caitra or Vaiśākha, having fed the officiating priests of the central group with brahmaudana boiled rice, he should give to each of them a thousand [cows].
While the offering to Pūṣan is spread out, or after it has concluded, he should release the horse; they should guard it according to the prescribed rule.

9.9.s: tisra iṣṭayaḥ sāvitryo bhavanti tāsu ssthitāsu dakṣiṇata āhavanīyasya hiraṇmaye kūrce prāṅmukha āsīno yajamānaḥ saṃvatsaramaharaharhotuḥ pāriplavamācakṣāṇasya śṛṇuyāt
9.9.d: तिस्र इष्टयः सावित्र्यो भवन्ति तासु स्स्थितासु दक्षिणत आहवनीयस्य हिरण्मये कूर्चे प्राङ्मुख आसीनो यजमानः संवत्सरमहरहर्होतुः पारिप्लवमाचक्षाणस्य शृणुयात्
9.9.m: There are three offerings to Savitṛ; when they have concluded, seated facing east on a golden bundle of grass to the south of the Āhavanīya, the sacrificer should listen day after day for a year to the Hotṛ reciting the cycle of revolving legends.
The Brahman and the Udgātṛ [sit] on a golden cushion, facing north.
He should give a hundred [cows] to the Hotṛ, ten to the Adhvaryu;
Or a thousand to the Hotṛ, a hundred to the Adhvaryu, and something to the other two.
His divine observances are as in the Rājasūya.
After the year, having tied up the horse, he should undergo consecration.
On that day, the priests should each take away these seats as their own.

9.9.s: tasya dvādaśa dīkṣā dvādaśopasadaḥ sarveṣāmahnāṃ bahirbahiṣpavamānaiḥ stuvīran
9.9.d: तस्य द्वादश दीक्षा द्वादशोपसदः सर्वेषामह्नां बहिर्बहिष्पवमानैः स्तुवीरन्
9.9.m: For it, there are twelve consecrations and twelve upasads; on all the days they should praise with outside bahiṣpavamāna chants.
On the middle day, having touched the horse's tail, they should glide forward for the bahiṣpavamāna chant.

9.9.s: sarpatsu yajamāna udgātāraṃ brūyāt udgātarapa tvāvṛṇe śatena ca niṣkeṇa cāśvo ma udgāsyatīti
9.9.d: सर्पत्सु यजमान उद्गातारं ब्रूयात् उद्गातरप त्वावृणे शतेन च निष्केण चाश्वो म उद्गास्यतीति
9.9.m: As they glide forward, the patron of the sacrifice should say to the udgātṛ priest: 'Udgātṛ priest, I dismiss you with a hundred and a gold coin; the horse will sing the udgītha for me.'
Having made the horse step into the place of chanting, they should show it a mare.

9.9.s: tāṃ yadābhikrandedatha yajamāna udgātāraṃ brūyādudgātarupa tvāhvaye śatena caiva niṣkeṇa ca tvameva ma udgāsyasīti
9.9.d: तां यदाभिक्रन्देदथ यजमान उद्गातारं ब्रूयादुद्गातरुप त्वाह्वये शतेन चैव निष्केण च त्वमेव म उद्गास्यसीति
9.9.m: When it neighs towards her, then the patron of the sacrifice should say to the udgātṛ priest: 'Udgātṛ priest, I invite you back with a hundred and a gold coin; you alone shall sing the udgītha for me.'

9.9.s: udañcamaśvamutkramayyāstāva upaviśyodgātāśvavratena stuyādabhi vājī viśvarūpa ityetāsu
9.9.d: उदञ्चमश्वमुत्क्रमय्यास्ताव उपविश्योद्गाताश्वव्रतेन स्तुयादभि वाजी विश्वरूप इत्येतासु
9.9.m: Having made the horse step out towards the north, and having sat down in the place of chanting, the udgātṛ priest should praise with the Aśvavrata melody on these [verses beginning]: 'The swift steed, possessing all forms...' [SV 2.1154].

9.9.s: hiraṇyakaśipunyāsīno bahiṣpavamānena stutvā sa eva taddharet
9.9.d: हिरण्यकशिपुन्यासीनो बहिष्पवमानेन स्तुत्वा स एव तद्धरेत्
9.9.m: Sitting on a golden cushion, having praised with the bahiṣpavamāna chant, he alone should take it.

9.10.s: yā patnīnāṃ priyatamā yajamānasya mā vāvātā rājaputrī
9.10.d: या पत्नीनां प्रियतमा यजमानस्य मा वावाता राजपुत्री
9.10.m: She who is dearest among the patron's wives is the favourite wife (vāvātā), a princess.

9.10.s: saṃjñapteṣu paśuṣu hotrābhimethite brahmā vāvātāmabhimethedūrddhvāmenāmucchrayatādgirau bhārharannivāthāsyai madhyame jatu śīte vāte punanniveti nirdiśet
9.10.d: संज्ञप्तेषु पशुषु होत्राभिमेथिते ब्रह्मा वावातामभिमेथेदूर्द्ध्वामेनामुच्छ्रयताद्गिरौ भार्हरन्निवाथास्यै मध्यमे जतु शीते वाते पुनन्निवेति निर्दिशेत्
9.10.m: When the victims are quieted and the hotṛ priest has addressed [his abuse], the brahman priest should revile the favourite wife: 'Raise her up, like one carrying a load on a mountain; then let her middle part receive [him], like one winnowing in a cool wind'—so he should point out.

9.10.s: śatamasyā rājanyānāṃ duhitaro'nucaryyaḥ syustāstaṃ pratyabhimetheyurūrddhvamenamucchrayatādgirau bhārharannivāthāsya madhyamejatu śīte punanniveti nirdiśeyuḥ
9.10.d: शतमस्या राजन्यानां दुहितरोऽनुचर्य्यः स्युस्तास्तं प्रत्यभिमेथेयुरूर्द्ध्वमेनमुच्छ्रयताद्गिरौ भार्हरन्निवाथास्य मध्यमेजतु शीते पुनन्निवेति निर्दिशेयुः
9.10.m: A hundred daughters of nobles should be her attendants; they should revile him in return: 'Raise him up, like one carrying a load on a mountain; then let his middle part receive [her], like one winnowing in a cool [wind]'—so they should point out.

9.10.s: udgātā parivṛktīmabhimethedyadasyā aṇuhota aṇusthūlamupātasan muṣkau yadasyā ejato gośaphe śakulā viveti nirdiśet
9.10.d: उद्गाता परिवृक्तीमभिमेथेद्यदस्या अणुहोत अणुस्थूलमुपातसन् मुष्कौ यदस्या एजतो गोशफे शकुला विवेति निर्दिशेत्

9.10.s: śatamasyāḥ sūtagrāmaṇīnāṃ duhitaro'nucaryyaḥ syustāstaṃ pratyabhimetheyuryaṃ devāso lalāmaguṃ prashṛṣṭinamājiṣuriti nirdiśeyuḥ sakthnā dediśyate nāryṛtasyākṣibhuvo yatheti
9.10.d: शतमस्याः सूतग्रामणीनां दुहितरोऽनुचर्य्यः स्युस्तास्तं प्रत्यभिमेथेयुर्यं देवासो ललामगुं प्रस्हृष्टिनमाजिषुरिति निर्दिशेयुः सक्थ्ना देदिश्यते नार्यृतस्याक्षिभुवो यथेति
9.10.m: A hundred daughters of charioteers and village chiefs should be her attendants; they should revile him in return: 'Whom the gods drove, a spotted steed, an impetuous one'—so they should point out—'the woman indicates with her thigh, like an eye-witness of the truth.'
Having touched water and sung the vāmadevya melody, they should mutter its verses.

9.10.s: svāhākṛtibhiścarite pūrveṇa sada upaviśya brahmodyaṃ vadeyuḥ
9.10.d: स्वाहाकृतिभिश्चरिते पूर्वेण सद उपविश्य ब्रह्मोद्यं वदेयुः
9.10.m: When the svāhākāra offerings have been performed, sitting to the east of the sadas hut, they should speak the brahmodya dialogue.

9.10.s: hotrādhvaryuṇā cokte brahmā pṛcchedudgātāraṃ pṛcchāmi tvā citayaṃ devasakha yadyattvamatra manasānuvettha yeṣu viṣṇustriṣu padeṣvaṣṭa yeṣu viśvaṃ bhuvanamāviveśeti
9.10.d: होत्राध्वर्युणा चोक्ते ब्रह्मा पृच्छेदुद्गातारं पृच्छामि त्वा चितयं देवसख यद्यत्त्वमत्र मनसानुवेत्थ येषु विष्णुस्त्रिषु पदेष्वष्ट येषु विश्वं भुवनमाविवेशेति
9.10.m: And when spoken by the hotṛ and the adhvaryu priest, the brahman priest should ask the udgātṛ priest: 'I ask you, who are conscious, O friend of the gods, whatever you know here with the mind; in which three steps did Viṣṇu stride, in which the whole universe entered?'

9.10.s: taṃ prati brūyādapi teṣu triṣu padeṣvasmin yeṣu viṣṇustriṣu padeṣvaṣṭa yeṣu viśvaṃ bhuvanamāviveśa sadyaḥ paryemi pṛthivīṃ dyāmute māmekenāṅgena divo asya pṛṣṭhamiti
9.10.d: तं प्रति ब्रूयादपि तेषु त्रिषु पदेष्वस्मिन् येषु विष्णुस्त्रिषु पदेष्वष्ट येषु विश्वं भुवनमाविवेश सद्यः पर्येमि पृथिवीं द्यामुते मामेकेनाङ्गेन दिवो अस्य पृष्ठमिति
9.10.m: He should reply to him: 'Even in those three steps in which Viṣṇu strode, in which the whole universe entered; at once I encompass the earth and this heaven, with one limb the back of this sky.'

9.10.s: udgātā pṛcchedbrahmāṇaṃ kisvidantaḥpuruṣa āviveśa kānyantaḥpuruṣe arpitānyetadbrahmannupabalihāmahe tvā kisvinnastvaṃ prativocāsyatreti
9.10.d: उद्गाता पृच्छेद्ब्रह्माणं किस्विदन्तःपुरुष आविवेश कान्यन्तःपुरुषे अर्पितान्येतद्ब्रह्मन्नुपबलिहामहे त्वा किस्विन्नस्त्वं प्रतिवोचास्यत्रेति
9.10.m: The udgātṛ priest should ask the brahman priest: 'What entered within man? What things are placed within man? This, O brahman priest, we offer as tribute to you: what will you answer us here?'

9.10.s: taṃ prati brūyāt pañcasvantaḥpuruṣa āviveśa tānyantaḥpuruṣe arpitānyetattān pratimanvāno asminna māyayā bhavasyuttaro maditi
9.10.d: तं प्रति ब्रूयात् पञ्चस्वन्तःपुरुष आविवेश तान्यन्तःपुरुषे अर्पितान्येतत्तान् प्रतिमन्वानो अस्मिन्न मायया भवस्युत्तरो मदिति
9.10.m: He should reply to him: 'Within five [elements] man has entered; those are placed within man. Considering these in reply to them, you are not superior to me by craft in this.'

9.10.s: sarve yajamānaṃ pṛccheyuḥ pṛcchāmastvā paramantaṃ pṛthivyāḥ pṛcchāmo yatra bhuvanasya nābhiḥ pṛcchāmastvā vṛṣṇo aśvasya retaḥ pṛcchāmo vācaḥ paramaṃ vyometi
9.10.d: सर्वे यजमानं पृच्छेयुः पृच्छामस्त्वा परमन्तं पृथिव्याः पृच्छामो यत्र भुवनस्य नाभिः पृच्छामस्त्वा वृष्णो अश्वस्य रेतः पृच्छामो वाचः परमं व्योमेति
9.10.m: All should ask the patron of the sacrifice: 'We ask you of the furthest end of the earth; we ask where the navel of the world is; we ask you of the seed of the vigorous horse; we ask of the highest heaven of speech.'

9.10.s: tān prati brūyādiyaṃ vediḥ paro antaḥ pṛthivyā ayaṃ yajño bhuvanasya nābhiraysomo vṛṣṇo aśvasya reto brahmāyaṃ vācaḥ paramaṃ vyometi
9.10.d: तान् प्रति ब्रूयादियं वेदिः परो अन्तः पृथिव्या अयं यज्ञो भुवनस्य नाभिरय्सोमो वृष्णो अश्वस्य रेतो ब्रह्मायं वाचः परमं व्योमेति
9.10.m: He should reply to them: 'This altar is the furthest end of the earth; this sacrifice is the navel of the world; this soma is the seed of the vigorous horse; this brahman is the highest heaven of speech.'
As the sacrificial fees for it, he should give a thousand on the first day, and likewise on the last.
On the middle day, whatever property belongs to non-Brahmins in a single realm, he should give that.
Or he should sacrifice in the middle of conquered [territory].

9.11.s: prācīhotre diśaṃ dadyāt dakṣiṇāṃ brahmaṇe'dhvaryave pratīcīmudīcīmudgātre yadanyakṣetrācca puruṣebhyaścetyubhayorvicārayoḥ
9.11.d: प्राचीहोत्रे दिशं दद्यात् दक्षिणां ब्रह्मणेऽध्वर्यवे प्रतीचीमुदीचीमुद्गात्रे यदन्यक्षेत्राच्च पुरुषेभ्यश्चेत्युभयोर्विचारयोः
9.11.m: He should give the eastern direction to the hotṛ priest, the southern to the brahman priest, the western to the adhvaryu priest, and the northern to the udgātṛ priest, as well as whatever is other than land and men, in both alternatives.
Or as much as they might say: 'We do not desire more than this.'

9.11.s: aṣṭācatvārśitaṃ vā madhyataḥ kāribhyaḥ sahasrāṇi dadyādekaikasmai caturviśatimarddhinībhyo dvādaśa tṛtīyinībhyaḥ ṣaṭ pādinībhyaḥ
9.11.d: अष्टाचत्वार्शितं वा मध्यतः कारिभ्यः सहस्राणि दद्यादेकैकस्मै चतुर्विशतिमर्द्धिनीभ्यो द्वादश तृतीयिनीभ्यः षट् पादिनीभ्यः
9.11.m: Or he should give forty-eight thousand [cows] to the chief priests, twenty-four [thousand] to each of those entitled to a half-share, twelve [thousand] to those entitled to a third-share, and six [thousand] to those entitled to a quarter-share.
These are the lowest limits, but he may give more at will.
He should arrange these very days as having fifteenfold stomas; that is the patantaka aśvamedha.
Having let the horse roam for half a month, he should sacrifice with this.

9.11.s: jyotiṣṭomo vai tasyātirātrastṛtīyamahaḥ syāt tena māsam
9.11.d: ज्योतिष्टोमो वै तस्यातिरात्रस्तृतीयमहः स्यात् तेन मासम्
9.11.m: An atirātra sacrifice on the model of the jyotiṣṭoma should be its third day; by that, for a month.
Or some third day of these [aforementioned] days should be of the standard archetype.
Or indeed, of the viśvajit, abhijit, vrata, or aptoryāma atirātra sacrifices.

9.11.s: teṣāstomacodanaiva syāt yathā catuṣṭomasarvastomayostrirātreṣu ca tantravilopo na vidyate
9.11.d: तेषास्तोमचोदनैव स्यात् यथा चतुष्टोमसर्वस्तोमयोस्त्रिरात्रेषु च तन्त्रविलोपो न विद्यते
9.11.m: [Objection:] Their prescription should concern the stoma alone, as in the case of the catuṣṭoma and the sarvastoma; and in three-day rites, no disruption of the ritual framework is found.

9.11.s: svatantrāstveva syuḥ kṛtalakṣaṇā hi purastāccodyante pratyakṣavikārātstomacodanā catuṣṭomasarvastomayoḥ
9.11.d: स्वतन्त्रास्त्वेव स्युः कृतलक्षणा हि पुरस्ताच्चोद्यन्ते प्रत्यक्षविकारात्स्तोमचोदना चतुष्टोमसर्वस्तोमयोः
9.11.m: [Reply:] But they should be independent [sacrifices], for their specific characteristics are prescribed beforehand; in the case of the catuṣṭoma and sarvastoma, the prescription of stomas occurs because of directly perceived modifications.
Disruption of the ritual framework occurs by explicit rule, just as the procedure for monotony in the sarvasvāra.

9.12.m: On the thirteenth day of the dark fortnight, he should be consecrated for the Jāmadagnya rite.
Its consecrations are twenty, and the upasads are twelve.
There, during the upasads, the adhvaryu priest should make separate oblations; the sacrificial cakes are stated by the Brāhmaṇa.
They have the same deity in the forenoon and afternoon.
These oblations begin with: 'May Agni accept the hotṛ's office...'
Having emerged from its concluding purificatory bath, he should sacrifice with the twelve-day iṣṭis.
In these, these very cakes are in reverse order.

9.12.s: vasiṣṭhasya janitre bhavata iti ssarpasya caturthe'hani bṛhatyanuṣṭubhoḥ pṛthaganupūrvamanukalpayeccaturthhi janitrasthānam
9.12.d: वसिष्ठस्य जनित्रे भवत इति स्सर्पस्य चतुर्थेऽहनि बृहत्यनुष्टुभोः पृथगनुपूर्वमनुकल्पयेच्चतुर्थ्हि जनित्रस्थानम्
9.12.m: 'There are two Janitras of Vasiṣṭha': on the fourth day of the gliding, he should arrange them separately in order on the bṛhatī and anuṣṭubh verses, for the fourth is the place of the Janitra.
There should be an option between the two according to the Ārṣeyakalpa.
In the Pañcaśāradīya rite, he should sacrifice with animal sacrifices on the seventh or eighth [tithi] in the fortnights of the month of Āśvayuja.
They should seize only heifers, and release the bulls.
As many of them as suffer mishap, that many others, not consecrated with yajus formulas, of similar appearance and of the same age, they should release.
In the sixth autumn, in the month of Kārttika, he should sacrifice.

9.12.s: tṛtīye ṣaḍrātre pañcamasyāhnaḥ pratyavarohīṇyukthāni syurityācāryyā abhyāsaṃghyo hyatra yathā devānāṃ pañcarātre
9.12.d: तृतीये षड्रात्रे पञ्चमस्याह्नः प्रत्यवरोहीण्युक्थानि स्युरित्याचार्य्या अभ्यासंघ्यो ह्यत्र यथा देवानां पञ्चरात्रे
9.12.m: In the third six-day rite, the ukthas of the fifth day should be descending: thus say the teachers, for there is a repetition here, as in the five-day rite of the gods.
'The descent there is produced by night': thus says Gautama; they should be only thirty-threefold.

10.1.m: In all sacrificial sessions, they should arrange the consecration, purchase [of soma], pressing [of soma], and concluding rising [of the sacrifice] in the bright half of the month.
If one of these cannot be accommodated, the purchase [of soma] should be in the dark half of the month.
If three [cannot be accommodated], only the concluding rising should be in the bright half of the month.
For these [sacrificial sessions], there are twelve consecrations and likewise [twelve] upasad days, when not specified otherwise.
And for those exceeding a year, the number of consecrations is according to desire.

10.1.s: prathame pañcadaśarātra ekānnaviṃśatirdīkṣā iti dhānañjayya ekāṣṭakā mahāvratamamāvāsyātirātra iti hyāheti
10.1.d: प्रथमे पञ्चदशरात्र एकान्नविंशतिर्दीक्षा इति धानञ्जय्य एकाष्टका महाव्रतममावास्यातिरात्र इति ह्याहेति
10.1.m: In the first fifteen-day sacrifice there are nineteen consecrations, says Dhānañjayya; for [the Brāhmaṇa] says: "The Ekāṣṭakā is the Mahāvrata, the new moon is the atirātra sacrifice."
Eighteen, says Gautama; for [the Brāhmaṇa] says: "The full moon is the atirātra sacrifice."
[Rites] beginning with the sixteen-day sacrifice and ending with the thirty-day sacrifice, as well as the forty-nine-day sacrifice, have eighteen consecrations.
Sacrificial sessions begin with the twelve-day rite.

10.1.s: tena yajetāpyahīnabhūtenāhīnaliṅgāni hyasmin brāhmaṇaṃ darśayati yathaikadīkṣaṇam
10.1.d: तेन यजेताप्यहीनभूतेनाहीनलिङ्गानि ह्यस्मिन् ब्राह्मणं दर्शयति यथैकदीक्षणम्
10.1.m: One may also sacrifice with that [twelve-day rite] as an ahīna sacrifice; for the Brāhmaṇa shows marks of an ahīna sacrifice in it, such as the single consecration.
On the first day, when using the Akṣāra as the brahman's sāman, one should perform it on the verses of the Audhasa.
Its [sāman] in uṣṇih metre should take the place of the one-syllable cadence, or the Audhasa [should do so].
However, there is no usage of [sāmans] based on bṛhatī in uṣṇih verses, and here most sāmans have cadences of more than one syllable.

10.1.s: tatra pauṣkalaṃ kuryāt jyotiṣṭomaprāyāṇi hyatra sāmāni
10.1.d: तत्र पौष्कलं कुर्यात् ज्योतिष्टोमप्रायाणि ह्यत्र सामानि
10.1.m: There one should perform the Pauṣkala; for here the sāmans are mostly those of the Jyotiṣṭoma.
